source.name: K2 BC Concordia Trek via Gondogoro La
source.summary: Take on one of the most epic and demanding treks on earth — a 20-day odyssey through the Karakoram's crown jewels via the legendary Gondogoro La high pass. Journey deep along the mighty Baltoro Glacier through a corridor of soaring granite towers to reach Concordia, the breathtaking amphitheater of 8,000m giants. Stand at K2 Base Camp, pay tribute at the Gilkey Memorial, then push higher over the formidable Gondogoro La at 5,610m — one of the world's most spectacular high-altitude crossings — descending through wildflower meadows and cedar valleys to Hushe. A truly once-in-a-lifetime adventure reserved for the bold and well-prepared.
highlights:
Trekking the legendary Baltoro Glacier: 62km of ice flanked by Cathedral Towers, Trango Towers and Gasherbrum IV
Reaching sacred Concordia at 4,650m: 360-degree panorama of four 8,000m peaks including the mighty K2
Visiting K2 Base Camp & Gilkey Memorial: tribute site to fallen climbers, vibrant expedition atmosphere in peak season
Overnighting at Broad Peak Base Camp: the closest and most dramatic face-to-face view of K2
Conquering the Gondogoro La at 5,610m: strenuous high-altitude crossing with unparalleled Karakoram panoramas
Descending through Dalzampa's field of flowers: wild roses, cedar, tamarisk and jagged glacial spires
Finishing through Hushe Valley: gateway village of legendary high-altitude porters and guides
source.itineraries:
Day 01: Islamabad 
Arrive in Islamabad. Meet guide & transfer to the hotel. In the morning take rest to recover from the long flight, in the afternoon Rawalpindi / Islamabad city tour. 
Sightseeing tour in Islamabad will consist of a selection of some of the following sites (depending on available time & your interests): the Faisal Mosque, the Government buildings 
on Constitution Avenue, the Shakar Parian Park with its rose and jasmine garden, the Pakistan Monument, the Lok Virsa heritage museum, Raja Bazaar area in Rawalpindi, Saidpur village Daman-e-Koh to look out over the twin cities. 
Overnight in Islamabad. 

Day 02: Islamabad – Skardu (2300m) 
Transfer to the airport for flight to Skardu. If the weather is clear we will have the opportunity to see some of the majestic mountains of the north from the airplane window incl. Nanga Parbat. In case of flight cancellation we will drive in two days on the famous KKH to Skardu. Trek briefing at Skardu Tourism Department either today or tomorrow. 
Optional: drive to Chilas and then add 2 days to visit Fairy Meadows. 

Day 03: Skardu 
Free day at leisure or drive to Skardu from Chilas. 
Optional sightseeing: Sadpara Lake, Skardu Bazaar, Kharpocho (Skardu) Fort.

Day 04: Skardu – Askoli (3000m) – Jhola (3140m) After breakfast proceed to Jhola in jeeps. It takes about six hours to drive from Skardu to Askoli. Askoli is the last village of Shigar valley, this used to be the starting point for the K2 Concordia trek but recently they have extended the road up to Jhola. The drive through the Braldu Gorge is guaranteed to knock your socks off! We will have lunch on the way, dinner will be in the camp, overnight in tents. 

Day 05: Jhola – Paju (3450m) 
We start on a relatively easy trail for 3 – 4 hours crossing Burdumal campsites along a 2 km stretched sandy river beach. After lunch continue towards Paju for another 2 – 3 hours trek. The trail climbs to a vantage point providing a view of the Snout of Baltoro. In the far distance you can see a magnificent panorama of the Cathedral Towers, Paju can be a crowded campsite. Overnight in camp. 

Day 06: Rest day at Paju (3450m) 
Rest day at Paju for local exploration. Enjoy the traditional music program and dancing by the local porters and other staff of the trekking teams. Overnight in camp. 

Day 07: Paju – Khuburse (3930m) 
Start trekking for 5 – 8 hours. Gradual climb of Baltoro Glacier on the Southern edge. After about 2 hours the path divides at the snout of Baltoro Glacier where the left branch goes to the Base camp of Trango Towers and the Serpo Liligo Pass. Continue to the right climbing up on to the glacier that stretches up the valley 62 km long and 2 km wide. Further 2 – 3 hours steady climb on a long diagonal to the other side. Follow the southern edge to Liliwa and onward to Khuburse – a lovely walk for about 90 min. to the campsite with clear water. Overnight at camp. 

Day 08: Khuburse – Urdukas (4050m) 
4 -5 hours walking, mostly along the crest of lateral moraine with stunning views of Paju Peak, Chorichi Biaho, Trango Tower and so on. Urdukas is a spectacular campsite. Overnight in a tent.

Day 09: Urdukas – Ghoro II (4380m) 
6 – 8 hours walking on a glacier. The first hour of our walk is across difficult terrain with many crevasses; however the way is smoother and easier in the middle. Continue 2 – 3 hours to Ghoro I opposite of Yermanendo Glacier, falling down from the Masherbrum Pass. For the next 3 – 4 hours continue east up the Baltoro Glacier following the telephone wire from Army HQ Ghoro to Gasherbrum IV. Ghoro II campsite is pitched on the rocks and ice in the centre of the glacier with water from the glacier melt. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 10: Ghoro II – Concordia (4650m) 
5 – 6 hours of relatively easy walking with spectacular views and gigantic mountain panorama, including Mustagata Tower, G IV, Matha Peak and the mighty K2. Camp at Concordia named by Martin Conway after the place Dela Concordia in Paris. Overnight in tent. 

Day 11: Concordia – Broad Peak BC (4850m) 
When we leave Concordia we first have to go through a more difficult part where two different glaciers (the Baltoro and Godwin- Austen glaciers) meet, then it is about a 3 hours fairly easy walk over the Godwin-Austen glacier to the base camp of Broad Peak. From the base camp you have an even more spectacular view of the K2 than from Concordia, we set up camp here, the rest of the day the group can take it easy and maybe get something from the different expedition groups. 

Day 12 – Broad Peak BC – K2 BC – Concordia (4650m) 
We leave early towards K2 base camp, about 3 hours walk, on arrival we visit the Gilkey memorial where deceased climbers are commemorated. In June and July there are many expeditions to the K2, the base camp will therefore be very lively and during the visit the group may get a bit of the "expedition atmosphere". After lunch we walk over the Godwin-Austen Glacier the same way back to Concordia (about 5 – 6 hours walk). 

Day 13: Concordia – Ali Camp Vigne Glacier (5010m) 
5 -6 hours continuous walk on Vigne Glacier, providing superb views of Chogolisa and Mitre peak. A rare mountain panorama and the camp will be just below the pass. Overnight in a tent.

Day 14: Vigne Glacier Ali Camp – Gondogoro La (5610) – Khuspang (4680) 
4 - 5 hours, we start very early in the morning for the strenuous and steep ascend to Gondogoro La (high pass), then another 3 – 4 hours descend to the high camp (Khuspang) on the other side. Also BC for Gondogoro Peak. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 15: Khuspang – Dalzampa (4300m) OR (RESERVE DAY) We can make this a reserve day, which means we can skip this part if required. 
From Khuspang to Saicho. 4 – 5 hours easy descend of glacier Moraine to the beautiful campsite of Dalzampa “field of flowers”. A climb to the lateral Moraine provides spectacular views of the glacier and jagged spires. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 16: Dalzampa – Shaicho (3330m) 
Another 4 – 5 hours walk on the lateral moraine through wild roses, gooseberry cedar and Tamarisk bushes. The Charakusa valley joins the Gondogoro at Shaicho and the route leads towards the base camp of K6 and K7. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 17: Shaicho – Hushe (3050m) – Skardu (2300m) This is the last day of the trek, for 4 – 5 hours we follow the east bank of the Hushe River on an easy path through the fields until reaching the village. From here we drive to Skardu by jeep and will make a short stop at Khaplu, the second largest kingdom of old Baltistan guarding the trade route to Ladakh along the Shyok River. Overnight at a hotel in Skardu. Trek debriefing at Skardu Tourism Department.

Day 18: Skardu – Chilas (or Naran) or Islamabad 
It’s time to say goodbye to the beautiful Baltistan region, today we drive to Chilas (or further to Naran) – a small bazaar town from where we can glimpse petroglyphs dating to the 1st century BC. Before reaching Chilas we will make some short photo stops, for example at the junction where the the 3 highest mountain ranges meet (The Himalayas, The Karakoram and The Hindu Kush) as well as at the Nanga Parbat viewpoint. 
In case of preference, it is possible (for the whole group) to fly to Islamabad instead of drive – 1 hour flight, rest of the afternoon can be spend at leisure. Transfer to Skardu airport for the flight to Islamabad, in case of flight cancellation we will drive to Chilas (or Naran) for 
overnight stay and next day onwards to Islamabad. 

Day 19: Chilas (or Naran) – Islamabad or Islamabad 
If the Babusar Pass is open then we will drive from Chilas via the Kaghan Valley and Naran towards Islamabad otherwise we will go over the famous Karakoram Highway (KKH) to Islamabad – this will be a full day of driving but the diverse scenery will make it a nice journey. On arrival in Islamabad we will have a nice farewell dinner and then take rest or have a full overnight stay in the hotel (depending on your flight departure time the next day). 
If we got a flight to Islamabad yesterday then we can spend today at leisure or have some additional sightseeing / souvenir shopping in Islamabad or (at extra charges) go for a day trip to Taxila to see the Taxila museum and various archaeological sites with remnants from the Buddhist Gandhara Kindgom. In case of flight cancellation on day 18 then today we will drive from Chilas to Islamabad. Farewell dinner and take a rest or full overnight stay in hotel. (depending on your flight departure time the next day). 

Day 20: Onward flight 
Midnight / early morning transfer to the airport for return flight home. End of Our Services –
We Hope You Had a Great Trip!

page.name: K2 Base Camp & Concordia Trek: Gondogoro La Crossing — 20 Days
page.subtitle: Alpine crossing of the Karakoram's highest passes — 62km Baltoro Glacier, Concordia amphitheater, and the Gondogoro La at 5,610m
page.summary: This 20-day trek traverses the Karakoram's most challenging high-altitude terrain, following the Baltoro Glacier 62 kilometers through a corridor of granite towers to Concordia at 4,650 meters, where four 8,000-meter peaks converge around K2. The route passes K2 Base Camp and the Gilkey Memorial, then climbs to the formidable Gondogoro La at 5,610 meters — a high pass requiring alpine fitness and acclimatization discipline — before descending through wildflower meadows and cedar valleys to the Hushe Valley. The itinerary demands strong trekking experience, high-altitude acclimatization, and proper preparation; weather, permits, and porter availability are subject to seasonal conditions and external factors beyond the operator's control.
highlights: Trekking the Baltoro Glacier: 62 kilometers of ice and moraine beneath Cathedral Towers, Trango Towers, and Gasherbrum IV
Standing at Concordia (4,650m): 360-degree panorama of K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I, and Gasherbrum II
Visiting K2 Base Camp and the Gilkey Memorial: tribute to climbers who died on the mountain, with active expedition activity in June and July
Overnighting at Broad Peak Base Camp (4,850m): elevated vantage of K2's north face across the Godwin-Austen Glacier
Conquering the Gondogoro La at 5,610m: strenuous high-altitude crossing with unparalleled Karakoram panoramas
Descending Dalzampa's flower meadows: lateral moraines lined with wild roses, cedar, tamarisk, and glacial spires
Finishing through Hushe Valley and Khaplu: traditional gateway villages of Baltistan's high-altitude porter and guide community
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Islamabad & Twin Cities Overview
Arrive in Islamabad and meet your guide for transfer to the hotel. The morning is reserved for rest and recovery from your flight. In the afternoon, visit Islamabad and Rawalpindi at a measured pace. Depending on your interests and available time, the sightseeing may include the Faisal Mosque, Government buildings on Constitution Avenue, Shakar Parian Park with its rose and jasmine gardens, the Pakistan Monument, the Lok Virsa heritage museum, Raja Bazaar in Rawalpindi, Saidpur village, and Daman-e-Koh for views across the twin cities. Overnight in Islamabad.

Day 2 — Islamabad to Skardu by Air
Transfer to the airport for a domestic flight to Skardu at 2,300 meters. Clear weather often permits views of Nanga Parbat and other northern ranges from the aircraft. In the event of flight cancellation, the route switches to a two-day overland journey via the Karakoram Highway. Trek briefing at the Skardu Tourism Department occurs today or the following day. An optional extension to Fairy Meadows via Chilas can be added with two additional days. Overnight in Skardu.

Day 3 — Rest Day in Skardu
Free day in Skardu. Optional sightseeing includes Sadpara Lake, Skardu Bazaar, and Kharpocho Fort. Overnight in Skardu.

Day 4 — Skardu to Jhola via the Braldu Gorge
After breakfast, a six-hour jeep journey departs for Jhola at 3,140 meters via Askoli. The road ascends through the Braldu Gorge, a steep and dramatic canyon, to Askoli — historically the trekking trail's starting point but now extended to Jhola by vehicle. Lunch occurs en route. Camp and overnight in tents at Jhola.

Day 5 — Jhola to Paju: Entry onto Baltoro
A relatively easy 5–7 hour trek begins across Burdumal campsites, following a sandy river beach for 2 kilometers. The route then climbs toward Paju at 3,450 meters over 2–3 hours. A vantage point near Paju provides views of the Baltoro Glacier snout and a distant panorama of the Cathedral Towers. Paju is a frequently crowded campsite. Overnight in tents.

Day 6 — Rest Day at Paju
Rest day at Paju for local exploration and acclimatization. The camp includes a traditional music and dance program by local porters and trekking staff. Overnight in tents.

Day 7 — Paju to Khuburse: Ascending the Baltoro Glacier
A 5–8 hour trek begins with a gradual climb along the southern edge of the Baltoro Glacier. After approximately two hours, the path divides at the glacier snout; the route continues right onto the main Baltoro, which stretches 62 kilometers long and 2 kilometers wide. A long diagonal ascent climbs to the glacier's far side over 2–3 hours. The southern edge is followed to Liliwa and onward to Khuburse at 3,930 meters, a 90-minute walk with clear glacial meltwater. Overnight in tents.

Day 8 — Khuburse to Urdukas: Lateral Moraine Traverse
A 4–5 hour walk follows the crest of lateral moraine, offering views of Paju Peak, Chorichi Biaho, and Trango Tower. Urdukas at 4,050 meters is a spectacular campsite. Overnight in tents.

Day 9 — Urdukas to Ghoro II: Upper Baltoro Crossing
A 6–8 hour glacier traverse begins with difficult, crevassed terrain for approximately one hour, then transitions to smoother ground mid-glacier. After 2–3 hours, Ghoro I sits opposite the Yermanendo Glacier, which descends from Masherbrum Pass. The route continues east up the main Baltoro for 3–4 hours, following an Army HQ telephone wire toward Gasherbrum IV. Ghoro II at 4,380 meters is a rocky and icy campsite in the glacier's center, with water from glacial melt. Overnight in tents.

Day 10 — Ghoro II to Concordia: Amphitheater of 8,000-Meter Peaks
A 5–6 hour relatively easy walk leads across the upper Baltoro with expanding panoramic views. Concordia at 4,650 meters lies at the convergence of multiple glaciers and opens to a 360-degree vista of K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II, and surrounding peaks. Named by mountaineer Martin Conway after the Piazza della Concordia in Rome, the site is a natural amphitheater. Overnight in tents.

Day 11 — Concordia to Broad Peak Base Camp
Departure from Concordia requires passage through difficult terrain where the Baltoro and Godwin-Austen glaciers meet. A 3-hour generally easy walk follows the Godwin-Austen Glacier to Broad Peak Base Camp at 4,850 meters. This elevated site offers an even more direct view of K2's north face than Concordia. The afternoon allows rest and informal interaction with other expedition groups. Overnight in tents.

Day 12 — K2 Base Camp Visit and Return to Concordia
An early departure leads to K2 Base Camp, approximately 3 hours distant. Upon arrival, the group visits the Gilkey Memorial, where fallen mountaineers are commemorated. During June and July, numerous climbing expeditions operate from the base camp, creating visible expedition activity and atmosphere. Following lunch, the return walk to Concordia retraces the Godwin-Austen Glacier over 5–6 hours. Overnight in tents at Concordia.

Day 13 — Concordia to Ali Camp: Vigne Glacier Approach
A 5–6 hour continuous walk on Vigne Glacier offers extended views of Chogolisa and Mitre Peak. The rare mountain panorama continues to expand. Ali Camp at 5,010 meters is positioned just below the Gondogoro La. Overnight in tents.

Day 14 — Crossing the Gondogoro La
An early start begins a strenuous 4–5 hour ascent to the Gondogoro La at 5,610 meters — a high-altitude pass requiring alpine fitness and proper acclimatization. The descent on the far side spans 3–4 hours to Khuspang at 4,680 meters, the high camp and base for Gondogoro Peak. Overnight in tents.

Day 15 — Khuspang to Dalzampa: Descent into Flower Meadows
A 4–5 hour easy descent follows lateral moraine from Khuspang toward the beautiful campsite of Dalzampa at 4,300 meters, known as a field of flowers. A climb to the lateral moraine provides views of glaciers and jagged spires. This day can function as a reserve day if conditions or group pace require additional time. Overnight in tents.

Day 16 — Dalzampa to Shaicho: Descent Through Cedar and Tamarisk
A 4–5 hour walk on lateral moraine descends through wild roses, gooseberry, cedar, and tamarisk scrub. The Charakusa Valley joins the Gondogoro at Shaicho at 3,330 meters, and the route heads toward the base camps of K6 and K7. Overnight in tents.

Day 17 — Shaicho to Hushe Valley and Return to Skardu
A 4–5 hour easy walk follows the east bank of the Hushe River through agricultural fields to the village of Hushe at 3,050 meters, marking the trek's final stage. A jeep transfer then travels to Skardu at 2,300 meters, with a brief stop at Khaplu, the second-largest historical kingdom of Baltistan, which guards the historic trade route to Ladakh along the Shyok River. Trek debriefing occurs at the Skardu Tourism Department. Overnight in a hotel in Skardu.

Day 18 — Skardu to Chilas or Islamabad
Today marks your departure from Baltistan. The group travels by jeep toward Chilas, a small bazaar town positioned near ancient petroglyphs dating to the first century BCE. The route offers several notable stops: at the junction where three of Asia's greatest mountain ranges converge—the Himalayas, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush—and at viewpoints overlooking Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth-highest peak. For groups preferring to fly, a one-hour domestic flight to Islamabad is available as an alternative to the full overland journey. Those choosing the flight arrive with the afternoon free for rest or independent exploration. Should the flight be cancelled, the group proceeds overland to Chilas for an overnight stay, continuing to Islamabad the following day.

Day 19 — Chilas to Islamabad via Karakoram Highway or Kaghan Valley
The final overland day departs Chilas toward Islamabad. If the Babusar Pass is open, the route traverses the Kaghan Valley and Naran, a scenic alternative. Otherwise, the famous Karakoram Highway is used, offering diverse landscapes over a full day of driving. Arrival in Islamabad is followed by a farewell dinner. Overnight accommodation at the hotel depends on the flight departure time the following morning. If a flight to Islamabad occurred on Day 18, today may be spent at leisure in the capital, with optional sightseeing, souvenir shopping, or a day trip to Taxila to visit the museum and archaeological sites of the Buddhist Gandhara Kingdom (extra fees apply). Overnight in Islamabad.

Day 20 — Departure
Midnight or early morning transfer to the airport for the return international flight. End of services.

page.name: Trishuli River Rafting — Nepal — 1 Day
page.subtitle: Four-hour run from Fishling to Mugling on Class III–IV rapids
page.summary: The Trishuli River, one of Nepal's primary rafting corridors, delivers a full-day run of intermediate whitewater between Fishling and Mugling — approximately 4 hours of paddling across Class III and IV rapids. The river cuts through foothills terrain marked by boulders, forested banks, and sections of open water suitable for swimmers and less experienced paddlers to find rhythm alongside more technical sections. Safety briefings and trained guides frame the progression, and the logistics—transport from Kathmandu, meal service on a riverbank beach, and onward connection to Pokhara or Chitwan—keep the experience contained within a single day.
highlights: Four-hour paddle on Trishuli River Class III–IV rapids between Fishling and Mugling
Guided whitewater navigation with trained rafting crew and full safety equipment
Riverbank lunch break on a sandy beach between paddle sections
Return logistics to Kathmandu, Pokhara, or Royal Chitwan National Park the same day

Day 1 — Trishuli River Rafting — Fishling to Mugling
Transport from Kathmandu begins in the early morning, covering approximately 3–4 hours of road to the put-in point at Fishling. Before entering the water, a comprehensive safety briefing covers equipment use, river navigation, and emergency protocol. The rafting guide and crew accompany the group throughout. The paddle itself covers roughly 4 hours downstream to Mugling, passing through Class III and IV rapids interspersed with calmer sections bordered by forest, rocky outcrops, and occasional open beaches. A lunch break takes place partway through on the riverbank. Upon reaching Mugling, participants can either return directly to Kathmandu or continue onward to Pokhara or Royal Chitwan National Park.

source.name: One day hike on Great Wall Mutianyu
source.summary:
Overview
Mutianyu Great Wall located in Huairou County 70 km northeast of central Beijing. The Wall of Mutianyu is connected with Jiankou in the west and Lianhuachi in the east. As one of the best-preserved parts of the Great Wall, Mutianyu section used to serve as the northern barrier defending the capital and the imperial tombs. First built in the mid-6th century during the Northern Qi, the Mutianyu section is older than the Badaling section of the Great Wall. During the Ming dynasty, under the supervision of General Xu Da, construction of the present wall began, building over the past wall. 



In 1404, a pass built in the wall. In 1569, the Mutianyu Great Wall rebuilt and till today most parts of it are well preserved. The Mutianyu Great Wall has the most significant construction scale and best quality among all sections of Great Wall. Follow your knowledgeable guide along the wondrous weave of the wall and marvel at the 2- or 3-story towers from ancient origins. Admire spectacular views of the Chinese countryside and gain a fascinating insight into this magnificent monument.  Sip bottled water and capture fantastic photographs throughout your exploration and note the perpetually changing perspective achieved by dipping gradients and steep inclines.
source.itineraries:
Day 1 Beijing – Mutianyu – Beijing (L)
Your guide comes and picks you up at your hotel in Beijing at 08:00Am. Travel to Mutianyu Great Wall in private van. The drive will take about 1. 5 hours. On arrival you will start to hike on the wall.

Follow your expert local guide to Mutianyu Great Wall. It will take you 30 mins walk up from entrance to enter the Wall. We will walk up to the Watchtower 8, takes about 30 mins staright up on the staris. Once we are on the Wall, we will do a loop walk from Watchtower 8 to Watchtower 20 and then come back to Watchtower 6. There are three options downhill: By walking, by Cable Car or by Tobaggan.

After the hike, we will head to local farmer's restaurant to have lunch. Meet and chat with the farmers over a home-cooked Chinese meal and learn the surrounding community developement. Then we will drive back to Beijing and drop you off at your hotel.

page.name: Mutianyu Great Wall: Day Hike from Beijing
page.subtitle: A day hike on one of the Great Wall's best-preserved sections, 70 km northeast of Beijing, with options for cable car or toboggan descent.
page.summary: Mutianyu, located 70 kilometers northeast of Beijing in Huairou County, represents one of the most intact stretches of the Great Wall. Built initially during the Northern Qi dynasty in the mid-6th century and substantially reconstructed under Ming general Xu Da, this section connected the capital's northern defense line with the imperial tombs. The wall's 2- and 3-story watchtowers rise across steep terrain, their preservation notably superior to many other accessible sections. A day hike here moves from the entrance through rising switchbacks to Watchtower 8, then traverses the wall itself via Watchtower 20 before circling back to Watchtower 6. The surrounding countryside reveals both the defensive logic of the wall's placement and the rural communities that have inhabited these slopes for centuries.
highlights: Hike through watchtowers 8 to 20 on the restored Ming-era wall structure
View the 2- and 3-story defensive towers built during the Northern Qi and Ming dynasties
Walk the loop section connecting Watchtower 20 and Watchtower 6 with views across the Beijing countryside
Lunch at a local farmer's restaurant with direct conversation with residents about regional development
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Beijing to Mutianyu: Wall Hike and Return
Your guide collects you from your Beijing hotel and drives by private vehicle to Mutianyu. Upon arrival, a 30-minute walk ascends from the entrance to reach Watchtower 8, where the formal wall begins. From there, the hike follows the restored Ming-era sections upward through Watchtower 20, then returns via a loop descending to Watchtower 6. This route covers the wall's best-preserved stretches, where 2- and 3-story towers overlook steep ravines and open countryside. The walk encounters significant elevation changes and narrow stair passages, particularly on the climb to Watchtower 8. Descent options include walking the same route, taking the cable car, or using the toboggan slide. Following the hike, you'll eat lunch at a local farmer's restaurant, where you can speak directly with residents about life in the surrounding communities. The return journey to Beijing takes place by vehicle, with drop-off at your hotel.

The day begins with a private vehicle transfer to the Terracotta Warriors and Horses Museum, located outside the city center. As evening settles, the route moves into the Muslim Quarter—a dense network of narrow streets and alleyways where restaurants, small food vendors, and family-run shops operate. The quarter represents centuries of settlement and commerce, and offers a direct view of how Xi'an's residents eat and move through daily life.

source.name: Kayak and Hike Wild Thailand
source.summary: This 10-day active journey moves through southern Thailand from city to jungle to island, entirely at ground level. It opens in Bangkok's Chinatown before a sleeper train carries you south into the wilderness. From there, the route threads through Khao Sok's ancient rainforest — on water, on foot and by bike — before reaching the limestone karst country of Krabi and the sheltered waters of Phang Nga Bay. Each day brings a different landscape and a different way to move through it: kayaking into sea caves, night hiking through jungle, climbing temple steps to panoramic summits, and paddling silently through mangroves where crabs scatter and macaques watch from the trees. It ends in Phuket Old Town after a final sea kayaking day across one of the most dramatic bays in Southeast Asia.
highlights:
Kayak the otherworldly Khao Sok Lake and circumnavigate the mangrove-fringed Ao Phang Nga National Park

Hike the jungle trails of Khao Sok National Park and Kao Yao Yai Island, and tackle the 1260 steps up to Tiger Cave Temple

Kick back in longtail boats, hang out on white-sand beaches spotting wildlife, then bed down in jungle lodges, floating bungalows and idyllic boutique hotels

Bangkok (Days 1–2)

Arrive in Chinatown — Yaowarat Road street food and Grand Palace on the doorstep
Cycling Bang Krachao — the "Green Lung of Bangkok," a lush island of trails and canals hidden inside the city
Local market lunch before boarding the overnight sleeper train south

Boat ride into Cheow Lan Lake — karst islands rising from turquoise water
Jungle trek to a viewpoint above the lake, staying in floating bungalows at sunset
Morning cycle through villages, rubber plantations and Wat Tham Pla (Fish Cave Temple)
Nocturnal jungle hike with a local guide — insects, wildlife and the forest at night

Kayaking through dense mangroves into caves decorated with stalagmites and ancient paintings
Gliding across shallow aquamarine lagoons to the ethereal blue pool of Tham Lord

Sacred trees, monks' sanctuary and the cave itself

Sunset cocktails and night market at Ao Nang

Speedboat to Koh Yao Yai inside Ao Phang Nga National Park
Kayaking through 5 sq km of mangroves near Ban Ya Mi village — fiddler crabs, macaques and undisturbed forest
Hiking with a local villager through jungle, rubber and coconut plantations

source.itineraries:
Day 1  Welcome to Bangkok
Touch down in Bangkok, the city with the world's longest name. It thrums with the pulse of old and new and is home to arguably some of the best street food in South East Asia. Soak up the vibes as you're collected by your host at the airport and transferred to your hotel in bustling Chinatown. Depending on when you arrive, head out to explore – Yaowarat Road, the main artery of Chinatown, is moments from your doorstep. Hit sights like the Grand Palace and its Emerald Buddha, or sample that fabled street food.

Day 2   Cycle Bang Krajao
Cycling Bang Krachao, Thailand
Cycling     2-3hrs · 15km
Head out of the frenetic streets of Bangkok as you are driven to Bang Krajao, where you'll hop on two wheels to explore winding trails. A lush haven known as the 'Green Lung of Bangkok', where nature thrives and languid canals cool the air; a leisurely cycle ride here is a tonic. Stop to sample food at the local market, and for a delicious lunch, before being driven back to the city to board your sleeper train. Roll out of Bangkok heading south to Surat Thani, where the adventure really begins.

Day 3   Khao Sok National Park
Hiking     3-4hrs · 5km · 250m up · 250m down
Wildlife Watching     1hr
Rolling into Surat Thani, grab your bag and fill up on breakfast. Hit the road by minibus to the sublime Khao Sok National Park, which conserves the largest area of virgin forest in southern Thailand and is teeming with native species. You’ll catch a boat for a scenic ride into the heart of Cheow Lan, a vast lake where karst islands jut out of turquoise waters. You’ll trek through the jungle on one of these islands to an amazing viewpoint of the lake (during the rainy season the hike to the viewpoint will be replaced with an alternative route or activity). At sunset, keep your eyes peeled for wildlife aboard a longtail boat, before bedding down on the lake in your tranquil floating bungalow.

Day 4    Khao Sok National Park
Cycling     2hrs · 20km
Wildlife Watching      2hrs · 4km
After waking up on the water, set off deep into Khao Sok National Park to your next destination, your jungle lodge nestled amidst one of the world's oldest rainforests. Hop on a bike and gently pedal your way along a network of small roads and tracks, passing villages and stopping at Wat Tham Pla ('Fish Cave') as well as a rubber and palm plantation. There'll also be time to stock up on refreshments and snacks from the local store. Chill for the afternoon before exploring the jungle after sunset, alive with the chorus of chirruping insects – an expert local guide will lead you on a nocturnal hike to discover wildlife. Later, drift off to the sounds of the forest symphony in your bungalow.

Day 5    Than Bok Khorani National Park
Kayaking     3-4hrs · 6km
Driving         2.5hrs
Head south to the small village of Bothor, on the coast of Phong Nha Bay, and into Than Bok Khorani National Park. Hop into a kayak and fully immerse yourself in this enigmatic place. Paddling through dense mangroves, you'll enter caves adorned with stalagmites, stalactites and ancient paintings. Glide across shallow aquamarine lagoons until you reach the ethereal blue pool of Tham Lord. Hit the beach or relax by the hotel pool for some late afternoon downtime, and savour the tranquillity of the location.

Day 6   Krabi
Hiking     3-4hrs · 5km · 600m up · 600m down
It's time to seek inner peace at the Tiger Cave Temple. Limber up and hit the 1260 uneven steps to the top, where you can take in the stunning views over Krabi province, presided over by the ever-watchful golden Buddha statue. Wander past sacred trees and the monks' sanctuary to the Tiger Cave itself. Afterwards, refresh yourself at Huay Toh, a glistening tiered waterfall at the base of Phanom Bencha mountain – the perfect place for a cooling dip. Relax at the hotel before catching a shuttle to lively Ao Nang for cocktails at sunset and a trip to the night market.

Day 7  Koh Yao Yai Island
Kayaking     3-4hrs · 4km
Leaving the mainland, travel to Koh Yao Yai by speedboat. The island sits within Ao Phang Nga National Park which is famous for its limestone cliffs and islets skirted by forest. Jump into a kayak to paddle quietly through unspoiled mangroves, watching fiddler crabs scuttle away from hungry macaques. The mangroves near Ban Ya Mi village cover an area of approximately five square kilometres, and are a critical part of the island ecosystem. After your paddle, enjoy a delicious lunch before relaxing into island life on the white sands and catching the sunset.

Day 8   Koh Yao Yai Island
Hiking      3hrs · 4km · 10m up · 10m down
Lace up your boots for a hike around Koh Yao Yai Island. Encircled by the clear coastal waters of Phang Nga Bay, soak up the charm of this peaceful location, away from the hustle and bustle. Head through lush jungle, on a hike led by a knowledgeable local villager. You’ll pass rubber and coconut plantations, spotting tropical birdlife hiding amid the foliage, and learn about their sustainable rubber tree oil extraction process. Enjoy lunch by a peaceful stream before heading on to the bustling vibes of Old Town Phuket, where you can explore at your own pace.

Day 9   Kayaking Phang Nga Bay, Thailand.
Kayaking      3-4hrs · 10km
Your final day features an epic sea kayaking adventure, visiting some of the most spectacular parts of Phang Nga Bay. Head to Ao Por pier to meet your local guide and be briefed on the day's activities, which will be tailored to the tides. Out on the water, you'll use a large longtail boat as a floating base. Circumnavigate tropical islands, discover hidden beaches and take in the gnarled limestone formations. Head ashore for a spot of lunch before a final paddle and to snorkel in the clear warm sea. Once back on dry land, have one final dinner with your fellow adventurers in the buzzing streets of Phuket Old Town.

Day 10    Phuket
After breakfast, say your final goodbyes. You'll be transferred to the airport in time for your flight home.

It begins in Bangkok's Chinatown before a sleeper train carries you overnight to Surat Thani. From there, the itinerary threads through Khao Sok National Park, where you kayak Cheow Lan Lake's turquoise waters, hike to jungle viewpoints, and spend a night in a floating bungalow. The route then sweeps through Than Bok Khorani's mangrove caves and stalagmite-lined passages, climbs 1,260 steps to Tiger Cave Temple's golden Buddha above Krabi province, and finishes with two days on Koh Yao Yai Island within Ao Phang Nga National Park—kayaking through mangrove forests where macaques watch from the canopy—before a final full day circumnavigating Phang Nga Bay's limestone islands and hidden coves by sea kayak.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Bangkok's Chinatown
Arrive in Bangkok and transfer to your hotel in Chinatown. Yaowarat Road, the neighbourhood's main artery, sits moments from your hotel—lined with street food stalls, vendor shops, and local activity. If your arrival allows, wander on foot: the Grand Palace and its Emerald Buddha are walkable from your hotel, as are the markets and restaurants in this working quarter. Settle in, rest if needed, and prepare for the journey south.

Day 2 — Cycling Bang Krachao, Bangkok's Green Lung
Leave central Bangkok behind and head to Bang Krachao, an island of wetland and forest within the city's administrative boundaries. You'll cycle approximately 15 kilometres on local trails, passing through residential areas and stopping at a local market for lunch. The terrain is flat and the pace is leisurely. Late afternoon, return to the city and board your overnight sleeper train heading south toward Surat Thani and Khao Sok National Park. Travel time: approximately 12 hours.

Day 3 — Boat and Jungle Trek to Cheow Lan Lake, Khao Sok National Park
Arrive in Surat Thani at dawn. After breakfast, travel by minibus to Khao Sok National Park, which conserves the largest area of virgin forest in southern Thailand and is teeming with native species. Catch a boat for a scenic ride into Cheow Lan Lake, where karst islands rise from turquoise waters. Hike to a viewpoint above the lake—approximately 5 kilometres with 250 metres of elevation gain—for views across the water to surrounding forested ridges. (During heavy rains, an alternative activity replaces this trek.) Sunset brings a wildlife-watching cruise aboard a longtail boat before settling into a floating bungalow for the night.

Day 4 — Cycling and Nocturnal Forest Walk, Khao Sok
Wake on the water and travel by minibus deeper into Khao Sok National Park to a jungle lodge. A morning bike ride covers approximately 20 kilometres over small local roads and tracks, passing through villages, rubber plantations, and coconut groves. Stop at Wat Tham Pla—Fish Cave Temple—a cave shrine fed by underground streams. Rest at the lodge in the afternoon. After sunset, a local guide leads a nocturnal hike through the forest canopy. Activity duration: approximately 2 hours. Terrain: uneven forest floor with roots and rocks.

Day 5 — Kayaking Than Bok Khorani and Mangrove Caves, Phang Nga Area
Travel south to a coastal location in the Phang Nga region. You'll kayak approximately 6 kilometres through dense mangrove passages, entering caves with stalagmites, stalactites, and historical rock art. Paddle through shallow lagoons until reaching a cave pool. Afternoon allows beach walks or rest at your accommodation. Transfer time: approximately 2 hours from Khao Sok.

Day 6 — Tiger Cave Temple and Huay Toh Waterfall, Krabi
Travel to Krabi province by road. Tiger Cave Temple sits on a mountainside above the city, accessed by 1,260 uneven steps. At the summit, a golden Buddha statue overlooks Krabi's landscape. The hike gains 600 metres in elevation and takes approximately 3–4 hours including time at the temple and adjacent meditation sanctuary. Descend and travel to Huay Toh, a multi-tiered waterfall at the base of Phanom Bencha mountain where a natural pool permits swimming. Evening brings a shuttle to Ao Nang for dinner and a visit to the night market.

Day 7 — Speedboat to Koh Yao Yai and Mangrove Kayaking
Travel by speedboat to Koh Yao Yai within Ao Phang Nga National Park. You'll kayak approximately 4 kilometres through mangrove forests near Ban Ya Mi village. The mangrove system covers roughly 5 square kilometres and forms part of the island's coastal ecosystem. Activity duration: approximately 3 hours. Terrain: calm mangrove channels; experience level: beginner to intermediate. Lunch is served before afternoon beach time and sunset viewing.

Day 8 — Island Hike with Local Guide, Koh Yao Yai
A local guide leads a hike through Koh Yao Yai's interior—approximately 4 kilometres over low-lying terrain through jungle, rubber plantations, and coconut groves. Activity duration: approximately 3 hours. Terrain: uneven forest trails. The walk includes explanation of rubber oil extraction, a primary livelihood for island residents. Lunch is taken by a stream before heading to Phuket Old Town.

Day 9 — Full-Day Sea Kayaking, Phang Nga Bay
Your final active day covers approximately 10 kilometres of sea kayaking in Phang Nga Bay. Meet your guide at Ao Por pier for a tide-and-weather briefing; the day's route adjusts based on conditions. A large longtail boat serves as a floating base. You'll kayak around tropical islands with limestone formations, land on beaches accessible by water, and snorkel in warm, clear water. Lunch occurs ashore. Activity duration: approximately 6–7 hours on the water. By evening, return to Phuket Old Town for a final dinner.

Day 10 — Departure from Phuket
After breakfast, transfer to Phuket International Airport in time for your onward flight. Transfer to the airport for your flight home.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Bentota
Private transfer from Colombo airport to Bentota, a coastal town on the south shore. Upon arrival in Sri Lanka our chauffeur will transfer you to Bentota, an interesting beach destination on the south coast of Sri Lanka. Bentota is sited on a lagoon system and has been a tourism destination since the colonial era. Check-in to a small beachfront hotel. Remainder of the day at leisure by the beach or within the hotel grounds.

Day 2 — Bentota Beach and Local Villages
A full day unscheduled for rest and swimming by the beach. In the afternoon, a guided walk through quaint settlements adjacent to Bentota, moving inland toward the edge of the Sinharaja Rainforest. This walk passes through working agricultural areas and fishing communities, offering a view of daily life and local land use. Return to the hotel by late afternoon. Accommodation in the same beachfront hotel.

Day 3 — Bentota to Galle and Yala
Transfer southward via the coastal road to Galle, a port town on the southwestern coast. Visit the Dutch Fortress, a 17th-century fortified compound built by the Dutch East India Company, with ramparts, cannons, and colonial-era architecture still intact. Proceed onward to Yala National Park, located in the southeast. The total driving time from Bentota to Yala is approximately 4 to 5 hours with the Galle stop. Check-in to a tented safari camp within or near the park boundary. Remainder of the day at leisure.

Day 4 — Yala National Park Safari and Local Fishing
Early morning guided safari into Yala National Park. The safari targets leopard and sloth bear sightings, though wildlife viewing cannot be guaranteed. Guides use 4x4 vehicles and track animals on foot. Safari duration is typically 4 to 5 hours. Return to camp for midday rest. In the late afternoon or early evening, participate in traditional fishing with a local fisherman on a lagoon or coastal waterway adjacent to the park, learning net casting and trap techniques. Accommodation in the tented safari camp.

Day 5 — Yala National Park Morning Safari
A second guided morning safari in Yala National Park, again targeting leopard and sloth bear. Timing and route may differ from Day 4 to increase sightings. Duration approximately 4 to 5 hours. Afternoon is at leisure or available for a lighter activity within or near the camp. Late afternoon transfer begins the northwestward journey toward Kitulgala, traveling inland away from the coast. Depending on route and road conditions, this leg takes 4 to 5 hours. Check-in to a small hotel near the Makandawa Rainforest border. Overnight in Kitulgala.

Day 6 — Canyoning and Rafting in Kitulgala
A full-day adventure combining a canyoning expedition into Makandawa Rainforest—jumping and sliding into natural pools—with white water rafting on River Kelani. Return to a stylish boutique hotel set by the rainforest border.

Day 7 — Departure
Your journey through Sri Lanka's natural wonders concludes. Reflect on time spent with family and lessons learned before your departure.

Day 8 — Trekking and Swimming in Knuckles Mountains
Trek through Knuckles Range cloud forest. Swim in a waterfall before settling into your luxury mountain camp for the night.

Day 9 — Trekking in Knuckles Cloud Forest
Full-day guided trek through the Knuckles Range, traversing cloud forest habitat at elevation. The route varies by guide choice and group fitness but typically includes ridge walks, descents into moss-covered valleys, and sections of dense vegetation where visibility is limited by persistent mist and cloud cover. Duration is 6 to 7 hours of active walking. A key component is a visit to a mountain waterfall where participants can swim in a pool fed by cascade. Return to the mountain lodge by late afternoon. Accommodation in the Knuckles.

Day 10 — Knuckles to Sigiriya by Cycling
Transition day involving a transfer from the Knuckles mountains westward toward the central plateau and then to Sigiriya, a journey of approximately 2 to 3 hours by vehicle. Upon arrival in the Sigiriya region, begin a guided cycling tour through rural villages, passing paddy fields, farming plots, and small lakes. Cycle through different village routes, passing through paddy and farming fields. Participants cycle on a mix of paved village roads and unpaved tracks. The cycling is interrupted by photo stops and brief village interactions. Late afternoon check-in to a small hotel in or near Sigiriya. Accommodation in Sigiriya.

Day 11 — Sigiriya Rock Fortress Ascent and Exploration
Early morning ascent of Sigiriya Rock, a 5th-century fortress and palace site rising approximately 200 meters above the surrounding plain. The structure was built by King Kasyapa and includes a network of stairs carved or constructed into the rock face, leading through defensive gates, landscaped terraces, and mirror wall galleries to the summit palace platform. The site contains frescoes, water features, and views across the central plateau. A guide contextualizes the archaeology and layout. Return to the hotel by midday. Afternoon at leisure or available for a lighter activity such as a visit to a nearby village or cultural site. Overnight in Sigiriya.

Day 12 — Cycling and Scenic Picnic near Sigiriya
A second day in the Sigiriya region. Cycle with villagers across rural villages passing paddy fields, farming fields and lakes all the way to Sigiriya Rock. The route culminates at a scenic viewpoint overlooking lakes and rural landscape. A picnic lunch is provided at this vantage point. Afternoon return to the hotel by vehicle. Remainder of the day at leisure. Accommodation in Sigiriya.

Day 13 — Transfer to Kalpitiya Peninsula
Transfer westward from Sigiriya toward the coast, traveling to Kalpitiya, a peninsula on the northwestern shore facing the Indian Ocean. Kalpitiya is known as a marine wildlife and fishing hub. Check-in to a beachfront property. Remainder of the day at leisure or spent exploring the beach and local surroundings. Accommodation in Kalpitiya.

Day 14 — Dolphin and Whale Watching from Kalpitiya
Early morning or midday boat-based marine excursion departing from Kalpitiya into the Indian Ocean. The trip aims to sight dolphins (spinner and bottlenose species are present seasonally) and whales (sperm whales and blue whales migrate through the region, particularly between November and March). Go for a Dolphin and Whale watching boat trip in the Indian Ocean. Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed. Guides identify species and explain marine ecology. Return to shore by late morning or early afternoon. Remainder of the day at leisure. Accommodation in Kalpitiya.

Day 15 — Coastal Cycling and Leisure in Kalpitiya
Cycle along the backroads of the area. Routes pass through fishing villages, lagoon edges, and agricultural plots. Time allows for stops and village interaction. Remainder of the day is unscheduled, available for swimming, rest, or informal exploration of the local area. A meal featuring local seafood can be arranged through the hotel but is not obligatory. Overnight in Kalpitiya.

Day 16 — Final Day in Kalpitiya
A full day at leisure in Kalpitiya. Options include swimming, beach walks, informal cycling, reading, or resting at the hotel. Optional activities such as an additional boat trip or a visit to a local fishing harbor can be arranged depending on interest and availability. Accommodation in Kalpitiya.

Day 17 — Departure
Transfer by private vehicle from Kalpitiya to Colombo International Airport. Depending on location of departure and check-out time, the drive takes 3 to 4 hours. Farewells and journey conclusion. The itinerary ends upon airport drop-off.

source.summary: Explore, hike, and cycle through India on this 15-day odyssey where every moment will feel like a dance between tradition and enchantment. You’ll wander the bustling streets of Delhi, where saris twirl in a vibrant dance of colours and the air is a tantalizing blend of exotic spices. Next, Agra and Pushkar await, with their bold forts and ancient temples spinning tales that echo through the ages. Ranthambore National Park invites you to discover animals roaming freely, peacocks putting on dazzling dance moves and maybe even a tiger or two. Pack your sense of wonder and let India unfold in all its glory.
highlights:
Guided tour of the Taj Mahal
Boat Safari on the Chambal River
Jeep Safari in Ranthambore National Park
Boat ride on Lake Pichola
Amber Fort Heritage Walk
Guided experience at Jantar Mantar Observatory
Visit Jodhpur's Mehrangarh Fortress
Visit Ranakpur Jain Temples in Udaipur
source.itineraries:
Day 1         Delhi: Welcome to India
From yoga to Bollywood, sacred temples to exotic wildlife, and bold textiles to complex vegetarian cuisine, experience every side of India in this incredible adventure that takes you through the very heart of Rajasthan. We welcome you to Delhi, and to India, and invite you to bring your curious nature to a country that is ready to inspire and impress. Get ready for a spirited and breathtaking two weeks.

You will be met at the airport by your included arrival transfer through the G Adventures-supported Women With Wheels project. After a welcome meeting with your CEO and group, go on an orientation walk and then head to a local restaurant for a welcome dinner.

Accommodation
The Metropolitan Hotel & Spa (or similar)
Meals included: Dinner
Day 2         Delhi: Historic & Modern India
Delhi, the vibrant capital of India, offers a captivating blend of rich history and modern tradition that charms every traveler. Set out on foot to discover a treasure trove of iconic landmarks such as the majestic Mehrauli Archeological Park, Humayun's Tomb and the intricate architecture of the India Gate, each narrating a story of India's diverse heritage. Delhi's bustling markets, divine cuisine and warm hospitality provide an immersive cultural experience, making it the perfect destination for the start of your trip.

Join your CEO on a walking tour of some of the oldest parts of Delhi, through ancient ruins and diverse religious sites. In the afternoon, discover Old Delhi and its narrow bylanes of Kinnari bazaar and the old havelis of Chandni Chowk. Wander through bazaars, spice markets and even ride a rickshaw to dive straight into daily life in India's biggest city.

        Namaste Delhi Walking Tour             Delhi   2h45m-3h
Visit G Values Fund project, Namaste Delhi. Start your walking tour of Qutab Complex and the Mehrauli archeological park. Go back in time as you walk through the oldest parts of historical Delhi and explore ancient ruins, monuments and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Wander through a park scattered with time-ravaged tombs and mosques.

        Old Delhi Guided Walk                      Delhi    4h-4h
Visit historic Old Delhi. Explore Jama Masjid, the "Great Mosque," and enjoy its massive courtyard, which can hold up to 25,000 worshippers. Also, visit the ancient Sikh temple of Gurdwara SisGanj, which was established in 1783.

Accommodation
The Metropolitan Hotel & Spa (or similar)Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast
Day 3         Agra: Taj Mahal & Agra Fort
No India itinerary is complete without a stop at two of the most iconic spots in the world, let alone India. The Taj Mahal and the Agra Fort are just a train ride away for today's adventure. The Taj Mahal is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World and a world renowned symbol of love and craftsmanship. And the legendary Agra Fort stands as a testament to the significance of India's grand Mughal Empire. We make sure these two world famous stops are checked off your India bucket list today.

After riding the train to Agra, visit both sites with your CEO and local guide. In the evening, drive to Dholpur and check into your OMG Stay- a tranquil set of stone cottages that feels a million miles away from the busy atmosphere of Delhi.

Taj Mahal Guided Tour                   Tāj Mahal   1h-3h
Here's one to cross off your bucket list: a visit to one of the Seven Wonders of the World. Take a guided tour of India's most famous landmark and an icon of Mughal architecture. Built by the emperor Shah Jahan as a testament of his love to his wife, Mumtaz Mahal, this stunning white marble structure draws visitors from all over the world.

Private Vehicle                   Agra – Dholpur    1h30m
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Train      Delhi – Āgra      2h-3h
Climb aboard, take a seat, and enjoy the ride.

Agra Fort Visit               Āgra    1h-3h
Enjoy a visit to this impressive Mughal fort made of red sandstone and white marble.

Meals included: Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner
Your OMG StayNarsingh Bagh
Day 4         Dholpur: Boating & Biking Safaris
You don't need to venture deep into the jungle to experience India's vibrant wildlife. Just outside of Dholpur, the chance to embark on a river safari showcases diverse landscapes and thriving wildlife. From spotting elusive species of birds and endangered animals to witnessing traditional riverside life, your time on the Chambal River will be unforgettable. If you're lucky, you may even spot a Gharial, a type of fish-eating crocodile. Hands inside the boat please!

After spending the morning on the river, the afternoon is dedicated to exploring the land. Get out on a bicycle to discover the lush jungle surrounding Narsingh Bagh, and join your guide in looking for a number of bird species local to the area.

Cycle Birding Tour     Dholpur    45m6km
Start later in the afternoon, riding on pedal bikes until Talab-E-Sahi with stops for birding and photography. Return to the hotel and afternoon tea (tea, coffee and cookies). There is no elevation gain in this cycle.

Chambal River Safari          Chambal River   1h-1h30m
Board the motor boats to cruise down the Chambal River. Take a chance spotting Migratory birds, wildlife along the banks or even the highly endangered Gharial, a large narrow-jawed crocodilian that mainly feeds on fish.

Meals included: Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner
Your OMG StayNarsingh Bagh
Day 5         Ranthambore: Iconic Safaris
From water to land, we continue the safari into Ranthambore National Park. This park is considered the best in the world to see the Royal Bengal Tiger in its natural habitat. Grab your binoculars and join your guide in search of not just tigers but leopards, bengal foxes, langurs and other amazing species. The magic of Ranthambore unfolds between dense forest and historical ruins offering an unparalleled safari experience.

Your Indian safari adventure continues as you leave Dholpur and drive to Ranthambore National Park. Spend the afternoon on safari before a delicious dinner at the lodge.

Private Vehicle       Dholpur – Ranthambore National Park   4h
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Ranthambore Afternoon Safari      Ranthambore National Park  2h-3h
Explore the park with local rangers on a safari drive in search of deer, birds, leopards, monkeys and, if you're lucky, elusive tigers.

Accommodation
Jungle Vilas Resort (or similar)Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner
Day 6         Jaipur: The Pink City
After another safari in Ranthambore, its onward to Jaipur. Jaipur isn't just known for its incredible history and monuments, it's also famous for being, well, pink! While the city is beautiful to gaze at, it's not just a pretty facade. Together we have the next two days to explore all this city has to teach us. First up, try your hand at block printing with the women of the Anoothi Project before an orientation walk through town.

After an early morning safari, you'll drive to one of the most colorful cities in India, Jaipur. Known for its colored gems and pink buildings, take it all in on a walking tour of the city.

Your G for Good Moment: Anoothi Block Printing Experience
Women from marginalised communities outside Jaipur came together to create the Anoothi Project. In Hindi, Anoothi means 'unique and extraordinary' and by teaching these women to master the traditionally male handicraft of block printing, the collective shines a light on the unique and extraordinary within each individual. At this G for Good visit, engage in a hands-on block printing activity with the local women as you indulge in some local snacks prepared by your hosts.

Ranthambore Morning Safari        Ranthambore National Park   3h-4h
Explore the park with local rangers on a safari drive in search of deer, birds, leopards, monkeys and, if you're lucky, those elusive tigers.

Jaipur City Tou
Take a brief tour of the city and use this as a chance to stretch your legs.

Private Vehicle     Ranthambore National Park – Jaipur    3h45m-4h15m   165km
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Accommodation
Narain Niwas Palace (or similar)Heritage Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast | Dinner
Day 7         Jaipur: Astrological Observations
Your Jaipur explorations start with the Amber Heritage walk. Step into what feels like a painting at the intricate Panna Meena before climbing onward to the majestically perched fortress of Amber Fort. The afternoon continues with a guided exploration of Jantar Mantar. This architectural wonder is marveled for its accurate observation of celestial bodies, showcasing the advanced astronomical knowledge of its time and the world's largest sundial.

Spend the morning exploring at Hawa Mahal and the Amber Fort. After lunch, take a special tour of Jantar Mantar, one of the most important astronomical observatories of the pre-modern world.

Hawa Mahal (Palace of the Winds)        Jaipur   15m-30m
Enjoy a visit to the intricately-carved Hawa Mahal, or "Palace of the Winds," which is named for the cool breeze that comes through the structure and keeps it comfortable, even in the hot Jaipur summers. Admire this architectural wonder and snap some photos.

Amber Heritage Walk           Jaipur   2h30m-3h
Visit the famous Panna Meena stepwell and the old temples around historic Amber Town before you make your way up to the fort.

Amber Fort Visit
Take in the Hindu and Muslim architecture of the beautiful Amber Fort. Wander through the halls and courtyards and admire the intricate details.

Jantar Mantar Visit                 Jaipur    1h-2h
Visit the Jantar Mantar observatory for a guided tour and explore the collection of astronomical instruments housed there, some dating back to 1727.

Accommodation
Narain Niwas Palace (or similar)Heritage Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast
Day 8         Pushkar: Your OMG Day
Today is jam packed with OMG worthy moments. Pushkar is one of the oldest and holiest cities in India and home to one of the only temples in the world dedicated to Brahma, the Hindu creator god. After a visit to this esteemed temple, you get the honor of choosing how the rest of your day unfolds. Connect with your spiritual side with a yoga class and a wellness and spirituality discussion or hike the famed pilgrimage path to Savitri Temple Hill and visit this picturesque hilltop. Come together in the evening again for sundowners with a show, to watch traditional Kalbeliya dancers alongside a local feast under the stars.

Your OMG Day starts in the holy town of Pushkar with a visit the famed Brahma Temple to meet a local pandit to understand and partake in ancient rituals. Then the choice is yours: choose to take an hour long yoga class followed by a wellness and spirituality discussion, or drive to the base of Savitri Temple hill for a hike up the 900 steps for a birds-eye view of Pushkar.

Traditional Dinner and Dancers
During sunset, enjoy the traditional Kalbeliya dancers and a sundowner. Engage in a traditional barbecue dinner experience under the stars admiring the starlit sand dunes of Pushkar.

Private Vehicle         Jaipur – Pushkar      2h30m-3h30m
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Pushkar Orientation Walk              Pushkar    1h3km
Join an orientation to explore key parts of this desert city, including beautiful lakes and ghats. Visit the famed Brahma temple, meet a local pandit and understand/take part in the ancient rituals

Your OMG Day: Yoga Class or Savitri Temple Hill Walk
Option 1: Take an hour long yoga class followed by a wellness and spirituality workshop.

Option 2: Take a short drive to Savitri Temple and walk up 900 steps to an amazing birds-eye view of Pushkar town. You'll go up 650 feet in elevation over a mostly paved path. The steps can be a bit uneven toward the top but the view is well worth it.

Accommodation
Atithi Luxury Resort (or similar)Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner
Day 9         Chandelao: The Age Old Fortress
The state of Rajasthan is famed for its historic forts and fortresses, handicrafts and its bright and beautiful block printing and tie-dye techniques. Textiles in India are more than just beautiful art, they're symbols of regional heritage, cultural identity and centuries of generational practices. Visit small hamlets whose traditions remained unchanged over the last hundred years, and overnight at a heritage property outside Jodhpur.

After a leisurely start to the morning, hop into jeeps to visit the small villages and hamlets outside Chandelao Garh, culminating in a visit to Pipar village to learn more about the 100 year old crafting techniques. An overnight in this unique heritage property awaits.

Private Vehicle               Pushkar – Chandelao   3h30m-4h
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Chandelao Fortress and Village    Chandelao    30m
Immerse yourself into the life of a tranquil Indian Village. Within the property, explore the old fortress where the historical family has resided for generations. Engage in a short understanding of the village and the history of Chandelao.

Pipar Village Visit                   Chandelao    1h30m
Ride in a jeep down to the hamlets of surrounding villages. Explore Pipar, a traditional rural town with 100 year old block and tie-dye printing techniques, and meet some of the families still practicing the craft.

Accommodation
Chandelao Garh (or similar)Guesthouse
Meals included: Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner
Day 10       Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fortress
It's almost impossible to say which is more beautiful: the view of Mehrangarh Fortress from the city of Jodhpur or the view of the Blue City of Jodhpur from Mehrangarh Fortress. The opportunity to visit and view both this morning will leave your heart full.

After a morning of discovery at the extraordinary Mehrangarh Fortress and the Blue City of Jodhpur, visit the Sunder Rang Cooperative and discover how this small social enterprise is helping more than 30 women and their families to provide meaningful support for their community. From textiles to handmade crafts, each unique item showcases the talent and creativity of the women who have made them.

Jodhpur Half-Day Tour                 Jodhpur    2h-3h
Explore the Blue City of Jodhpur with a half-day tour. You will visit Mehrangarh Fort, a breathtakingly beautiful fort located at the top of a cliff, which offers a stunning view of Jodhpur below. Learn about the many battles fought there and get a sense of what it was like to be Rajasthani royalty by visiting its well-stocked museum. Then continue on to Jaswant Thada, a memorial with unparalleled views over the city.

Mehrangarh Fort Visit                               Jodhpur
Visit this breathtakingly beautiful fort located at the top of a cliff, which offers a stunning view of the Blue City of Jodhpur below. Learn about the many battles fought there and get a sense of what it was like to be Rajasthani royalty by visiting its well-stocked museum.

Your G for Good Moment: Sunder Rang Cooperative Visit
Visit the Sunder Rang cooperative and meet the ladies who run the project. Sunder Rang is a craft market run by local women. It offers the chance to buy some of the finest clothing, jewelry and souvenirs. Currently more than 35 women and their families are being impacted by this non profit organisation which helps them market their products. Apart from paying them fair wages, the organisation shares 60% of the profit with the families and keeps 40% for other activities like health, sanitation and eduction of the women in the village.

Accommodation
Chandelao Garh (or similar)Guesthouse
Meals included: Breakfast | Dinner
Day 11        Udaipur: City of Lakes
From one town to the next, India seems to become more and more spectacular. Continue to Ranakpur Jain Temple to observe one of the most magnificent marble temples in India. After exploring the temple, continue to the romantic lakefront city of Udaipur. There's no better welcome to a waterfront town than dinner at one of the finest lakefront restaurants.

Together the group drives to Ranakpur to visit the famous Ranakpur Jain Temples before reaching Udaipur. After an orientation walk of the old city, enjoy a group dinner at a lakeside restaurant. Stretch your legs on walk along the lake or take a tuk tuk back to your hotel for the night.

Private Vehicle           Chandelao – Ranakpur     3h30m160km
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Ranakpur Jain Temples Visit             Ranakpur     1h-2h
Enjoy a visit to this magnificent white marble temple devoted to Adinath, a god in the Jain religion. Jains believe in "ahimsa," non-violence to all living beings. Built in the 15th century, the temple has 1444 individually carved pillars.

Private Vehicle                    Ranakpur – Udaipur    2h30m90km
Settle in and scan the scenery from the convenience of a private vehicle.

Udaipur Orientation Walk                              Udaipur
Go on a guided orientation walk and get to know local markets and key places.

Accommodation
Fateh Niwas by Fateh Collection (or similar)Heritage Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast | Dinner
Day 12        Udaipur: Famous Lakes & Ancient Hills
Udaipur, the City of Lakes, invites you to rise and shine with a bike ride to start the day. Enjoy incredible views with a gentle bike ride through the ancient hills of Udaipur to Badi Lake where breakfast will be waiting. After an exhilarating start to the day, join your CEO to tour the palace complex and Jagdish Temple, which has been welcoming worshippers since 1651.

This afternoon is at leisure to explore as you please. Grab a tea at a cafe or do some exploring on foot with your camera. In the evening, climb aboard for a sunset boat ride to explore Lake Pichola.

Badi Lake Breakfast Cycle                    Udaipur   2h-3h12km
Cycle to Badi Lake through Udaipur village tracks on a traditional bike. Arrive to Badi Lake and enjoy breakfast on the bank.

Jagdish Temple Visit                             Udaipur
Visit the intricately-carved Jagdish Temple, which pays homage to Vishnu, the Hindu god of preservation. Make sure to take a peek at the black stoned image of Vishnu that's housed inside the shrine.

Pichola Lake Boat Tour                      Udaipur     1h-2h
Sit back and relax on this amazing boat tour on Pichola Lake. The views of the city and gorgeous palaces, including City Palace, are unparalleled.

Accommodation
Fateh Niwas by Fateh Collection (or similar)Heritage Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast
Day 13        Mumbai: The City of Dreams
Mixed with modern high rises and old world architecture, Mumbai is India's financial and cinematic capital. This afternoon will take you to some of best spots in all of Mumbai like Dhobi Ghat, Asia's largest open-air laundromat, and Malabar Hill.

After a relaxing morning with some leisure time in Udaipur, your flight takes you to the busiest city in all of India, Mumbai. Take a driving tour of the city after your arrival before reaching the hotel.

Airport Transfer                            Udaipur – Udaipur Dabok
You will be met at the hotel and transferred to the airport.

Plane                             Udaipur – Mumbai     1h15m-1h15m
Look! Up in the sky! It's a bird! It's a plane! It's... yup, it is a plane, actually.

Airport Transfer          Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport – Mumbai
Drive from the airport to our hotel. En route make photo stops at the Dhobhi ghat, Asia's largest open air laundromat. Drive up Malabar Hill to the hanging gardens for a birds-eye view of the bay from on top of the city's oldest reservoir, covered by a topiary garden. Continue down through Marine Drive popularly known as "the queen's necklace" before reaching your hotel.

Accommodation
Trident, Nariman Point, Mumbai (or similar)Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast
Day 14        Mumbai: Elephanta Caves
A scenic escape from the bustling city brings you to the island of Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Walk through rock carved columns to enter the impressive caves dedicated to Lord Shiva. These incredible carvings date back to the 5th century, and represent a sacred site for Hindu believers.

Visit the Gateway of India before you board your private boat to Elephanta Caves. Travel for an hour to reach the UNESCO World Heritage site. Spend a half-day visiting these rock-cut stone temples that date back to the 5th century. The afternoon is at your leisure to relax, eat, shop, or all three! This evening, join your CEO and fellow travellers for one final farewell feast.

Farewell DinnerMumbai
Join your group for one last dinner together.

Gateway of India Visit                              Mumbai1h-2h
Enjoy a visit to this architecturally splendid arch, popular with tourists from India and around the world. It was built during the British rule and offers amazing views of the Arabian Sea, with boats bobbing in the water close by.

Excursion of Elephanta Cave                      Mumbai   4h-4h
Visit the Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The collection of cave temples are located just off the shore of Mumbai, on Elephanta Island, and contain a series of sculptures and carvings depicting Hindu symbols.

Accommodation
Trident, Nariman Point, Mumbai (or similar)Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast | Dinner

Your adventure has come to an end, you can depart at any time.

Departure Day
Not ready to leave? Your CEO can help with any onward travel arrangements you require.

Meals included: Breakfast

page.name: Northern India: Taj Mahal, Forts & River Safaris — 15 Days
page.subtitle: Delhi to Mumbai via Agra, Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur, with safaris on the Chambal River and in Ranthambore National Park
page.summary: This 15-day itinerary moves through northern India's principal architectural and natural landmarks, beginning in Delhi and concluding in Mumbai. The route traces colonial and Mughal heritage through Agra's Taj Mahal and Fort, follows the Chambal River by boat near Dholpur, enters Ranthambore National Park for wildlife safaris, and examines the astronomical instruments at Jantar Mantar in Jaipur. The journey incorporates village visits in Rajasthan, textile workshops in Chandelao and Jodhpur, the marble temples of Ranakpur, lakefront stays in Udaipur, and concludes with the rock-cut caves of Elephanta Island near Mumbai. Throughout, the trip includes guided walks in historic quarters, interactions with artisan communities supported by nonprofit initiatives, and transfers by private vehicle, train, and domestic flight.

Boat safari on the Chambal River searching for gharials and migratory birds

Mehrangarh Fortress overlooking Jodhpur's blue-painted old city

Sunrise cycle to Badi Lake in Udaipur with breakfast
