page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Delhi
Arrival in India. You will be met at Delhi airport by your included arrival transfer.

Once settled at your accommodation, The Metropolitan Hotel & Spa (or similar), you will meet your trip leader and fellow travellers for an orientation meeting. This provides an opportunity to connect with the group and receive information before the adventure.

The afternoon includes an orientation walk through Delhi's streets. As evening falls, you will head to a local restaurant for a welcome dinner with your group.

Meals included: Dinner

Day 2 — Delhi: Mehrauli Archaeological Park and Old City Bazaars
Begin your Delhi experience with a morning walking tour through Mehrauli Archaeological Park, one of the city's oldest quarters. The park contains ancient ruins, tombs, and historic mosques across its grounds, each structure marking different periods of Delhi's history. You will walk through the Qutab Complex alongside your trip leader, moving through centuries of architectural history.

In the afternoon, navigate Old Delhi's narrow bylanes and markets. Visit Kinnari Bazaar and the historic havelis of Chandni Chowk. The Jama Masjid, known as the Great Mosque, dominates this section with its large courtyard, with capacity for up to 25,000 worshippers. Visit this structure alongside the Gurdwara SisGanj, a Sikh temple established in 1783.

Ride an auto-rickshaw through the spice markets and narrow commercial streets to observe daily trading activity and community commerce.

You will stay at The Metropolitan Hotel & Spa (or similar). Breakfast is included.

Day 3 — Train to Agra: Taj Mahal and Agra Fort
A train departing Delhi travels south to Agra, approximately 2–3 hours. Upon arrival, a guided tour of the Taj Mahal is included. Built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, this white marble structure is a monument of Mughal architecture. Your trip leader and local guide will provide architectural and historical context during the tour.

After the Taj Mahal, the group visits Agra Fort, constructed from red sandstone and white marble. This fort documents the reach and organization of the Mughal Empire.

In the afternoon, a private vehicle carries the group on a 90-minute drive to Dholpur. You will stay at Narsingh Bagh, a collection of stone cottages providing accommodation outside the city activity.

Day 4 — Dholpur: Chambal River Safari and Bicycle Birding
The morning begins with a motorboat safari on the Chambal River, 1–1.5 hours in duration. The landscape is observed from the water, with migratory birds present along the banks. Gharials (narrow-jawed crocodilians) inhabit the river, and the area shows traditional riverside settlement.

The afternoon includes a 6-kilometer bicycle route with no elevation gain, departing from Narsingh Bagh to Talab-E-Sahi through surrounding jungle. A guide leads stops for bird observation and photography. The route is accessible for all cycling levels. Return to the hotel for afternoon tea.

Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are included.

Day 5 — Ranthambore National Park: Tiger and Leopard Safaris
A four-hour private transfer from Dholpur delivers you to Ranthambore National Park. Upon arrival, you will stay at Jungle Vilas Resort before heading out for an afternoon safari.

Your jeep safari, 2–3 hours in duration, is led by local rangers through dense forest interspersed with historical ruins. Wildlife in the park includes Bengal tigers, leopards, Bengal foxes, wild boar, langurs, and various deer species. Tiger sightings are not guaranteed. Return to the lodge as daylight fades.

Day 6 — Ranthambore Safari to Jaipur: Pink City Arrival and Block Printing Workshop
The day begins before dawn with an early morning safari through Ranthambore National Park, 3–4 hours in duration, led by local rangers. Departure for Jaipur follows the safari.

The drive to Jaipur spans approximately 165 kilometers, requiring 3 hours 45 minutes to 4 hours 15 minutes by private vehicle.

Upon arrival in Jaipur, a brief walking orientation introduces the city's layout and its distinctive pink-coloured buildings.

A hands-on block printing activity is included at a local artisan workshop, where you will learn block printing techniques and receive local snacks prepared by your hosts.

You will stay at Narain Niwas Palace, a heritage hotel. Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Day 7 — Jaipur: Amber Fort, Panna Meena Stepwell, and Jantar Mantar
Your Jaipur exploration begins with a walking tour that includes the Panna Meena stepwell and Amber Fort, a fortress perched on elevated terrain showcasing Hindu and Muslim design elements throughout its halls, courtyards, and chambers.

Before heading to Amber Fort, visit the Hawa Mahal, or Palace of the Winds. Its distinctive honeycomb façade features small windows. The carved pink sandstone is photographable.

After lunch, a guided tour of Jantar Mantar includes an astronomical observatory containing a collection of astronomical instruments, some dating to 1727. The complex houses the world's largest stone sundial. Walking among these structures provides information about pre-modern astronomical observation and calculation.

You will stay at Narain Niwas Palace or a similar heritage hotel.

Day 8 — Pushkar: Brahma Temple, Optional Activities, and Desert Sunset with Traditional Dancers
A 2.5–3.5 hour private drive from Jaipur delivers you to Pushkar, one of India's oldest cities. The city is home to a temple dedicated to Brahma, the Hindu creator deity.

Your morning begins with a guided orientation walk through Pushkar's landmarks, including lakes and ghats. At the Brahma Temple, you will meet a local pandit who guides you through ritual practices.

The afternoon offers two options:
Option 1: A one-hour yoga class followed by a wellness and spirituality discussion.
Option 2: A visit to Savitri Temple, accessed via 900 steps climbing 650 feet in elevation along a mostly paved path. The ascent becomes uneven toward the summit and provides views across Pushkar and the surrounding desert landscape.

As daylight approaches dusk, the group reconvenes on sand dunes for refreshments and a cultural performance. Traditional Kalbeliya dancers perform as the sun descends. A barbecue dinner follows.

Accommodation is at Atithi Luxury Resort or similar. Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Day 9 — Chandelao: Historic Fortress and Village Textile Traditions
A 3.5–4 hour private drive from Pushkar brings you to Chandelao, a small settlement anchored by an ancient fortress. The property has been home to the same family for generations.

After settling in, a jeep excursion takes you into surrounding hamlets, culminating in Pipar village. Families here practice block printing and tie-dye techniques that have been largely unchanged for over a century. Conversations with the artisans reveal how these methods persist in rural India.

You will stay at Chandelao Garh, a heritage property within the fortress grounds. Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Day 10 — Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fortress and the Blue City
The morning includes a half-day exploration of Jodhpur city and Mehrangarh Fortress, which sits at the summit of a dramatic cliff. Its honey-coloured stone walls contain a museum documenting the fortress's strategic importance across centuries of Rajasthani history. From the ramparts, the Blue City unfolds below in its distinctive palette. The tour includes Jaswant Thada, a marble memorial located nearby.

In the afternoon, visit a local craft enterprise operated by women, producing textiles, jewelry, and handmade items. This visit provides opportunity to understand community-based production and to purchase items directly from producers.

You will stay at Chandelao Garh or a similar guesthouse. Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Day 11 — Ranakpur's Marble Temples and Udaipur's Lakefront
The journey begins with a 3.5-hour drive from Chandelao across 160 kilometers. Ranakpur Jain Temples are white marble structures devoted to Adinath, a central deity in the Jain faith. The main temple features 1,444 individually carved marble pillars, each distinct, supporting the sanctuary. These pillars reflect the Jain principle of ahimsa, non-violence toward all living beings.

After exploring the temple complex, the route continues south toward Udaipur, another 2.5-hour drive across 90 kilometers. Upon arrival, a guided orientation walk leads through the old city's winding lanes, introducing local markets and key landmarks. The day concludes with a group dinner at a lakeside restaurant.

You will stay at Fateh Niwas by Fateh Collection. Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Day 12 — Udaipur: Badi Lake Cycle, Jagdish Temple & Pichola Lake Sunset
Start before dawn with a 12-kilometer bicycle ride through Udaipur's ancient hills and village tracks to Badi Lake, taking 2–3 hours on a traditional bike at a gentle pace. Breakfast is provided on the lake's bank.

Return to the city for a guided visit to Jagdish Temple, built in 1651. The shrine features intricately carved stonework and a black stone image of Vishnu housed within. Your trip leader will provide context on the temple's role in the city's spiritual life.

The afternoon is unscheduled, allowing time for independent exploration of the city.

As evening approaches, board a boat for a 1–2 hour tour on Lake Pichola. The water reflects the city's palaces, most notably the City Palace, and the hills beyond.

You will stay at Fateh Niwas by Fateh Collection.

Day 13 — Flight to Mumbai: Dhobi Ghat, Malabar Hill, and Marine Drive
After a relaxed morning in Udaipur, depart on a flight of 1 hour 15 minutes to Mumbai. Upon arrival at Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport, an airport transfer takes you directly into a driving tour.

The route includes a photo stop at Dhobi Ghat, where hundreds of workers wash textiles daily by hand in orderly rows of concrete tanks. The drive ascends Malabar Hill to the Hanging Gardens, a topiary-covered reservoir. From here, the vantage point offers views across the Arabian Sea and the bay below.

The tour descends through Marine Drive, a curved coastal road, leading to your hotel, the Trident at Nariman Point (or similar).

Breakfast is included.

Day 14 — Elephanta Caves and Gateway of India
Begin the day at the Gateway of India, an architecturally splendid colonial-era arch built during British rule. This monument overlooks the Arabian Sea.

From here, board a private boat for a one-hour journey to Elephanta Island, home to a UNESCO World Heritage site. The island's cave temples were carved into rock during the 5th century and were dedicated to Lord Shiva. Walking through the columned passages, you will encounter sculptures and carvings depicting Hindu iconography and cosmology.

A half-day visit allows time to move through the caves at a deliberate pace.

The afternoon is yours to structure as you wish—rest at your accommodation, visit local markets, or enjoy a meal. As evening settles, join your trip leader and fellow travellers for a farewell dinner.

Day 15 — Departure from Mumbai
Your adventure concludes today. Depart at a time that suits your schedule. Breakfast is included before you leave. Your trip leader remains available to assist with any onward travel arrangements you may require.

source.name: Kuari Pass Trek
source.summary:
Winter Kuari trek is one of the most beautiful winter trek that perfectly capture the grandeur of the snow-landscape. Settled at an altitude of 4264 meters, Kuari Pass boasts of amphitheatre views of Kamet (7756m), Trishul (7120m), Chaukhamba (7128m), and the great divine peak of Nanda Devi (7817m) and its twin Nanda Devi East (7434m). The mountain pass is located in the Garhwal region of the state of Uttarakhand. It lies to the south of the Tibetan Plateau, and is within the enchanting Nanda Devi National Park. Well-known as the Lord Curzon trail, Kuari Pass Trek gives you a chance to view the impressive blue-skyline donned with white landscape.

The trek will start from Joshimath, and will proceed to Akhod Getta which will be your first campsite. The charismatic view of the snow-dressed mountain, Mt. Chaukhamba will be seen from the base camp. Moving on to the goal destination, the trail of Kuari Pass will have great patches of snow and the blowing winds will make the trek even more exhilarating. After walking past snow-covers, you will reach the peak point of Kuari Pass that will offer spectacular views of Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat. The trek isn’t over, as your next destination goal will be the fascinating Auli. The track to reach Auli is laden with dense forests that houses great diversity of flora and fauna, and vast pasturelands. The stupendous views of Auli Himalayan peaks, Nanda Devi, Hathi Ghodi peak and Dronagiri will make your heart drool with its beauty.

Explore another version of Kuari Pass trek
source.itineraries:
Day 1: Drive from Haridwar – Joshimath (260 km)​
After arriving in Haridwar, you will drive to Joshimath, a religious city for people going to Badrinath and Hemkund Sahib. The drive will take around 10 hours covering a distance of 260km for you to reach. On reaching, you will check-in at your pre-booked hotel.
Day 2: Drive from Joshimath to Dhak Village (10 Kms) - Trek from Dhak to Akhod getha (6Kms)​

Today morning you will embark your journey for Kuari Pass trek. At first you will have to drive to Dhak village, from where you will walk and snake through beautiful rhododendron, oak and hemlock forest. After walking for a while, you will descent to a grassland which will also be your campsite at Akhod Getha. The magnetizing view of the snow-dressed mountain, Chaukhamba can be seen from your campsite. You will also come across shepherds living here who come down during harsh winters. Strike a conversation with a local, and you will get to hear numerous stories about the place. You will also find a spring line at the crown of the meadow for unlimited water supply. Take pictures of the sweeping mountains, sit at the edge gazing the beauty of nature or take pleasure in the company of your friends midst the beautiful landscape.
Day 3: Trek from Akhod Getha to Kuari Pass to Akhod Getha (10 kms)​

As soon as the morning unfolds, you will set out to continue your trek to Kuari Pass. Post breakfast, your trek leader will give you tips and tricks about the following trek, listen carefully and abide by it throughout the trek. You will trek for 5km, however, in between you will take breaks as the trail today will be quite steep. A trek will ascend till Khullara, from where you will encounter great patches of snow. After walking past the snow covers, you will reach the Kuari top. The winds won’t stop whispering, while you will take in the sweeping vistas of the mighty Himalayas. After clicking pictures of Mt. Nanda Devi, you decent back to the campsite, Akhod Getha and relish your hot dinner at night, post which you spend time with your friends or rejuvenate yourself midst the nature.
Day 04: Trek from Akhod Getha to Gulling (5 Kms)​
Wake up to the beautiful sunrise, and head-out for the next campsite, Gulling. Leaving behind the vistas of Mt. Chaukhamba, you will see Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat when you reach the next base camp. On arriving at the campsite, you can relax in your tent or can choose to indulge in various activities. At night, you will be served with tantalizing dinner, post which you either sleep or spend time with your friends.
Day 05: Trek from Gulling to Auli via Gorson Bugyal (08 Kms) - Drive to Joshimath form Auli (15kms)​

After savouring your breakfast midst natural surroundings, today you will trek to Auli. The magnificent views of Auli will spell-bind you with its splendour. The trail to Auli will meander through dense forests and vast pasturelands. While trekking you will outstanding views of Himalayan peaks, Nanda Devi, Hathi Ghodi peak and Dronagiri. On the way, click pictures of the ravishing valleys, villages till you reach the lush grassland of Gorson. Cross the grasslands, and continue walking till your reach the verdant meadows of Auli. On reaching Auli, you will be served with hot lunch, after relishing the food, you will take your belongings and drive back to Joshimath
Day 06: Joshimath to Haridwar
Today is the last day of your trip, as after having breakfast, you will drive back to Haridwar taking along ample of memories. You can indulge in evening Aarti at Harki Pauri if you arrive in time. Later, you can spend the rest of the time at your leisure.

page.name: Kuari Pass Trek: Winter Ascent to 4,264 Meters
page.subtitle: Six days across Garhwal's high-altitude pass, connecting Joshimath to Auli through snow fields and rhododendron forest
page.summary: The Kuari Pass trek crosses the high-altitude frontier between the Hindu pilgrimage towns of the Alaknanda Valley and the skiing meadows of Auli. The pass itself sits at 4,264 meters on the southern flank of the Tibetan Plateau, within Nanda Devi National Park, and commands a direct amphitheater view of five major Himalayan peaks: Nanda Devi (7,817m), Kamet (7,756m), Chaukhamba (7,128m), Trishul (7,120m), and Nanda Devi East (7,434m). The route, historically known as the Lord Curzon trail, ascends from the forested slopes above Joshimath through rhododendron and hemlock stands, then climbs into open meadow and snow fields to the pass itself, before descending into the high grasslands of Auli. Winter conditions—significant snow cover and sustained wind—define the character of the trek.
highlights: Ascent to Kuari Pass with direct views of Nanda Devi and four other peaks
Rhododendron and oak forest trekking through Akhod Getha meadow, first camp in the trek
Snow-field crossing with views of Chaukhamba, Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat
High-altitude grassland descent to Auli via Gorson Bugyal, an alpine meadow
Winter alpine terrain: snow patches, high wind exposure, and thin-air acclimatization
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Drive from Haridwar to Joshimath
The trek begins with a 260-kilometer drive from Haridwar, a major city and railhead in the foothills, to Joshimath, a pilgrimage center on the Alaknanda River. Joshimath is the traditional starting point for journeys to Badrinath and Hemkund Sahib. The drive takes around 10 hours, climbing steadily into the Garhwal region. Hotel accommodation in Joshimath for the night.

Day 2 — Dhak Village to Akhod Getha Meadow
A 10-kilometer drive from Joshimath brings you to Dhak Village, where the Kuari Pass trek formally begins. From here, the trail winds through dense rhododendron, oak, and hemlock forest, following traditional shepherd routes through the landscape. After approximately 6 kilometers of walking, the forest gradually opens into Akhod Getha, a sweeping alpine meadow that will serve as your first campsite. The magnetizing views of snow-dressed Chaukhamba dominate the northern horizon from here. You may encounter local shepherds who inhabit these meadows seasonally, descending during the harshest winters. A conversation with them often reveals stories woven into the landscape itself. A spring line runs along the crown of the meadow, providing reliable water supply. Take time to photograph the surrounding peaks, sit at the meadow's edge to absorb the vastness of the terrain, or simply rest in the company of fellow trekkers amid this beautiful alpine setting.

Day 3 — Kuari Pass Day Trek from Akhod Getha
After breakfast, your trek leader will brief you on the day ahead—listen carefully to their guidance on managing the steep terrain. The 5-kilometer ascent to Kuari Pass climbs steeply toward Khullara, where snow patches begin to dominate the landscape. As you gain elevation, wind exposure increases noticeably. The final push brings you to Kuari Pass at 4,264 meters, where the vista opens dramatically: Nanda Devi and Nanda Devi East rise to the northeast, Kamet anchors the north, while Chaukhamba and Trishul frame the western horizon. Take time to absorb the scale of these mountains before retracing your steps back to Akhod Getha. The descent returns you to camp in the late afternoon. Settle into the evening with a hot dinner, then spend time with fellow trekkers or simply rest beneath the open sky.

Day 4 — Akhod Getha to Gulling Meadow
The trek descends to Gulling, a secondary meadow campsite. Views shift from Chaukhamba (left behind to the south) to the broader northern panorama of Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat. The terrain remains open grassland with sections of remaining snow. Tented accommodation at Gulling.

Day 5 — Trek to Auli via Gorson Bugyal, then Drive to Joshimath
After breakfast, you'll trek 8 kilometers through dense forests and expansive pasturelands toward Auli. The trail ascends through changing terrain, passing through Gorson Bugyal's lush grasslands before reaching the verdant meadows of Auli. Throughout the walk, the Himalayan peaks dominate the northern horizon—Nanda Devi, Hathi Ghodi, and Dronagiri visible across the valleys. Pause to photograph the ravishing landscape and villages along the way. On arrival at Auli, lunch awaits before you drive the 15 kilometers back down to Joshimath, where you'll spend the night.

Day 6 — Joshimath to Haridwar
Your final day begins with breakfast before the 260-kilometer drive back to Haridwar, a journey of approximately 10 hours. If timing permits upon arrival in late afternoon or evening, you may join the Aarti ceremony at Harki Pauri. The remainder of the day is at your leisure.

highlights:
Hike Three of Taiwan's Stunning Historic Trails
Deep experience with indigenous hosts at workshops, village visits and classes
Visit some of the biggest temples and night markets in Taiwan
Taste-of-Place culinary and tea tasting experiences
source.itineraries:
Day One: Taipei (Arrival Day)
Arrive in Taipei and explore the city, including a 300-year-old temple. Enjoy a group welcome dinner as the city lights up, followed by a stroll through a vibrant shopping district.

Day Two: Caoling Historic Trail | Hualien
Hike the 7km Caoling Historic Trail, a 200-year-old trade route. Enjoy coastal views and a visit to Daoist Temple before a transfer to Hualien. Explore Dadongmen Night Market at night.

Day Three: Indigenous Wild Greens | Liyu Lake | Shoufeng
Visit the Indigenous Wild Vegetable Center showcasing the Amis people's efforts in preserving wild vegetable species. Lunch lake side at Liyu Lake, followed by a flat 5km walk around the lake (mostly designated car-free path).

Day Four: Hunter's School | Kiwit Village | Ruishui
Visit a local Hunter's School and learn about the Amis' hunting culture and cuisine. Enjoy a short walking tour with herbal foot bath in Kiwit. Hot spring hotel in Ruisui.

Day Five: Dye Workshop | Tea Tasting | Yuli Hot Springs
Get hands-on at the Ruisui dye workshop creating your own keepsake. After lunch, enjoy a honey-flavored black tea tasting before ending the day at a historic hot spring hotel.

Day Six: Walami Trail | Bunan House | Chishang
Explore the Batongguan Historic Trail, once the site of Japanese-indigenous conflict. Epic suspension bridges, central mountain views, and visit a remote Bunan slate house.

Day Seven: Calligraphy Writing | Amis Cooking | Taitung
Join local elders to learn about rice harvesting traditions. Experience the joy of calligraphy and its connection to the land. Enjoy an evening Amis cooking experience.

Day Eight: Alangyi Historic Trail | Mudan Hot Springs
Hike Taiwan's last undeveloped coastline. This easy coastal hike, Alangyi, weaves together Indigenous, Japanese, and Taiwanese history. Overnight at a hot spring hotel in Mudan.

Day Nine: Sandimen | Buddhist Temple | Taipei
Heading off from our hotel, we'll visit a glass bead cultural workshop in Sandimen before lunch. After lunch, we'll head to Fo Guang Buddhist Temple before taking the High Speed Rail back to Taipei.

Day Ten: Taipei (Departure Day)
Leisurely breakfast and any last minute souvenirs or snacks before jumping on our airport transfer back to Taoyuan International Airport. Say farewell to Taiwan until next time!

page.summary: This ten-day route moves through Taiwan's eastern spine—a region most international visitors skip in favor of Taipei and the west coast. The itinerary anchors on three historic trails: the 7-kilometer Caoling trade route, the Batongguan path through Japanese-era conflict sites, and the Alangyi coastal walk along Taiwan's least developed shoreline. Between treks, the trip centers on hands-on engagement: dye workshops in Ruisui, calligraphy and rice-harvesting instruction from local elders, cooking classes with Amis hosts, and extended time at the Indigenous Wild Vegetable Center and Hunter's School. Three nights are spent in hot spring hotels in Ruisui and Mudan. Accommodations throughout are mid-range to upscale regional properties. A licensed bilingual guide leads all activities; private van transport handles the route. The trip departs and concludes in Taipei.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Taipei and Temple Visit
Arrive at Taoyuan International Airport and transfer to Taipei. Visit a 300-year-old temple in the city center, then gather for a welcome dinner as evening lights emerge. Stroll through a lively shopping district to close your first night.

Day 2 — Caoling Historic Trail to Hualien
Hike the 7km Caoling Historic Trail, a 200-year-old trade route with coastal views and a Daoist Temple stop. Transfer to Hualien for the evening, then visit Dadongmen Night Market on foot.

Day 3 — Indigenous Wild Vegetables and Liyu Lake Walk
The morning focuses on the Indigenous Wild Vegetable Center near Liyu Lake, where the Amis people work to preserve local vegetable species and traditional food knowledge. After a lunch beside the lake itself, a flat 5-kilometer walk circles Liyu Lake on a mostly car-free designated path. The route is unhurried and offers time to observe the landscape and local activity around the water.

Day 4 — Hunter's School and Kiwit Village
A visit to a local Hunter's School in Kiwit Village introduces Amis hunting practices and the seasonal cuisine they sustain. A short walking tour follows, including time for an herbal foot bath. The day ends with a transfer to Ruisui, where you stay at a hot spring hotel with direct access to thermal pools.

Day 5 — Dye Workshop, Tea Tasting, and Hot Springs
The Ruisui dye workshop gives hands-on experience with traditional dyeing methods; you create an item to take home. After lunch, a black tea tasting—focused on honey-flavored regional varieties—introduces the local tea culture. The evening returns to the hot spring hotel, where thermal baths and spa facilities are available.

Day 6 — Batongguan Historic Trail and Bunan Slate House
Walk the Walami Trail through sites of Japanese-indigenous conflict. Major suspension bridges span ravines with central mountain views. Visit a remote Bunan slate house, a traditional stone dwelling. End in Chishang.

Day 7 — Rice Traditions, Calligraphy, and Amis Cooking in Taitung
Learn rice-harvesting customs from local elders, then practice calligraphy and its connection to the land. An evening Amis cooking class visits traditional food preparation with regional ingredients.

Day 8 — Alangyi Historic Trail and Mudan Hot Springs
An easy coastal hike along Taiwan's last undeveloped shoreline, tracing Indigenous, Japanese, and Taiwanese history. Evening transfer to Mudan for an overnight stay at a hot spring hotel.

Day 9 — Glass Bead Workshop, Buddhist Temple, and Return to Taipei
The day begins in Sandimen with a visit to a glass bead cultural workshop, where artisans produce beads using traditional techniques specific to Paiwan communities. Lunch follows in the village. The route then moves north to the Fo Guang Buddhist Temple, a major regional religious complex. From there, the High Speed Rail carries you back to Taipei, arriving by evening.

Day 10 — Departure from Taipei
A leisurely breakfast precedes any final shopping or snacking before the airport transfer to Taoyuan International Airport and departure.

source.subtitle: 555km & 8400m Elevation | White Sand Beaches | KOM | Hot Springs
source.summary:
At 555km and 8400 meters of elevation, this is a tour for those wishing to truly test themselves on two wheels!
Carefully crafted from years of experience, this 5-stage route highlights why Taiwan is fast becoming Asia's top cycling destination. Expect challenging climbs, quiet roads, flowing descents, and stops at hot spring. Feast on a variety of cuisines, from Hakka and Han to Aboriginal. This unforgettable cycling adventure ends with a glass of champagne on the white sand beaches of Kenting.
highlights:
Ride from Taipei to the southern tip along the 'spine' of Taiwan
Cycle up the famed Taiwan KOM Challenge route
A day off to enjoy the beauty of Sun Moon Lake
Experience Aboriginal culture and delicious cuisine
Visit some of Taiwan's best known temples
Incredible 50km+ descents, amongst the longest in the world
Finish your trip with a couple of days at Taiwan's premier beach town
source.itineraries:
Day One: Taipei - Yilan (109km / 221m / 5 hrs)
Riding from southern Taipei, we quickly reach the countryside. The morning has steady climbs, while the afternoon levels out along a jade river winding along a deep gorge. Passing through Chatianshan Nature Reserve; today features little traffic and lots of views. Though challenging in parts, the descent and a soak in wild hot springs makes it worthwhile.

Day Two: Yilan - Lishan (75km / 2633m / 4.5 hrs)
Today features a ride up the first 3/4 of the world famous Taiwan KOM Challenge 2024 route. A beautiful and iconic cycling route. Take your time and enjoy the views along a road that is quiet and remote. We will arrive at Lishan in the afternoon, check in and enjoy a well-earned celebratory meal.

Day Three: Lishan - Sun Moon Lake (110km / 2081m / 5.5 hrs)
The climbing starts almost straight the hotel, as we take on the last kilometres of the Taiwan KOM Challenge. Today's summit, Wuling (3275m) is the island's highest passable point. From here, we follow a 50km descent – and it is as exhilarating as it sounds! We head up to Sun Moon Lake, one of Taiwan's most iconic destinations and the largest lake in the country.

Day Four: Sun Moon Lake (Rest Day)
Today is a well-deserved rest day, with a chance for guests to relax at the hotel, visit some of the cultural sites including pagodas, temples or enjoy a unique tea-tasting experience.

Day Five: Sun Moon Lake - Alishan (128km / 2699m / 6.5 hrs)
Another challenging day in the saddle awaits as we climb towards Jade Mountain! This is a stunning climb day with breathtaking views, terraced tea fields and rice paddies! We roll into Alishan Township at the end of the day, which sits high on the central plateau in Taiwan's famous tea country.

Day Six: Alishan - Qishan (126km / 1570m / 5 hrs)
Today we move off the Central Mountain Range and down towards the plains of the southwest. A morning of descents takes us past the Tsengwen Reservoir, before finishing at Qishan Old Street, a busy market renowned for its street vendors & historic buildings with baroque-style facades.

Day Seven: Qishan - Kenting (122km / 456m / 4.5 hrs)
Today is the final ride day. We head through the southern countryside along to a coastal road and finally into the tropical resort town of Kenting, an area famed for its stunning beaches and crystal blue seas. A must is a glass of champers on the beach to celebrate the end of this wonderful tour!

Day Eight: Kenting - Taipei (Non-Riding Day)
After a leisurely morning, breakfast and a final swim in the ocean, the group will pack up and transfer back to Taipei in private transportation for the end of the tour.

page.name: Taiwan's Mountain Spine: 555km Cycling from Taipei to Kenting
page.subtitle: Eight days of high-altitude climbing, 50km+ descents, and remote mountain roads across Taiwan's central ridge.
page.summary: This eight-day cycling route traces Taiwan's mountain spine from Taipei to the southern coast—555 kilometers at 8,400 meters of cumulative elevation. The journey follows five distinct stages, including most of the Taiwan KOM Challenge route, which summits Wuling at 3,275 meters, the island's highest passable point. Days alternate between long climbing stages and extended descents; a rest day at Sun Moon Lake breaks the physical demands midway. The route passes through tea country, Aboriginal regions, and lowland farmland before finishing on Kenting's beaches. Overnight stops include mountain towns, resort areas, and cultural centers, with meals ranging from Hakka and Han regional cooking to Aboriginal specialties.
highlights: Ride the Taiwan KOM Challenge route, summiting Wuling at 3,275 meters
Descend over 50 kilometers from Wuling to Sun Moon Lake in a single day
Rest and visit Sun Moon Lake, Taiwan's largest lake, with access to historic pagodas and tea tastings
Climb through terraced tea fields and rice paddies toward Alishan Township on the central plateau
Pass the Tsengwen Reservoir and historic Qishan Old Street with baroque-style market buildings
Finish with two days at Kenting's beaches and tropical resort setting
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Taipei to Yilan: Gorge Roads and Hot Springs
The route departs southern Taipei into the countryside, climbing steadily through the morning before the terrain levels into afternoon riding along a jade river that winds through a deep gorge. The Chatianshan Nature Reserve provides most of the day's scenery on a road with minimal traffic. Late afternoon brings a descent to lower elevation and a soak in wild hot springs.

Day 2 — Yilan to Lishan: Taiwan KOM Challenge Begins
The famous Taiwan KOM Challenge route begins here. This 75-kilometer stage climbs 2,633 meters over the first three-quarters of the challenge course—a quiet, remote road that gains elevation steadily through the afternoon. Arrival in Lishan comes as the day's light fades, followed by a celebratory meal at the hotel.

Day 3 — Lishan to Sun Moon Lake: Wuling Summit and the 50km Descent
Climbing resumes immediately from the hotel as the route tackles the final kilometers of the KOM Challenge, reaching Wuling at 3,275 meters—Taiwan's highest passable summit. From the peak, a 50km descent follows to Sun Moon Lake, one of Taiwan's largest lakes.

Day 4 — Sun Moon Lake: Rest Day
A full day off. Guests can remain at the hotel or wander nearby cultural sites, including pagodas and temples, or participate in a tea-tasting experience at one of the lakeside facilities.

Day 5 — Sun Moon Lake to Alishan: Tea Country Climbing
This 128-kilometer stage climbs 2,699 meters toward Jade Mountain through Taiwan's famous tea country. Terraced tea fields and rice paddies line the ascending road. The route ends at Alishan Township, situated on the central plateau at high elevation, after a full day of climbing with sustained views across the surrounding highlands.

Day 6 — Alishan to Qishan: Descent to the Plains
The route leaves the Central Mountain Range, descending 1,570 meters over 126 kilometers toward the southwestern plains. Morning descending passes the Tsengwen Reservoir before the route flattens into the lowlands. The day ends at Qishan Old Street, a busy market district known for street vendors and historic baroque-style buildings.

Day 7 — Qishan to Kenting: Final Coastal Ride
The last full riding day covers 122 kilometers through southern countryside and along the coast to Kenting, Taiwan's main beach resort. Elevation gain is minimal—only 456 meters across the day—as the route moves through farmland before reaching the tropical setting of Kenting's renowned beaches.

Day 8 — Kenting to Taipei: Final Morning and Return
After a leisurely morning and a final swim in the ocean, the group enjoys breakfast before packing up. Private transportation then carries everyone back to Taipei, bringing the tour to a close.

source.name: Highlights Of Thailand
source.summary: This is a Thailand trip jam-packed with experiences and destinations that ventures beyond where other trips go. Thailand's stunning beauty and charismatic culture are ever present on this ExoAsia adventure - discover the exquisite 'Land of Smiles' in style. Thailand conjures up images of spicy delicacies, majestic elephants, golden Buddhas, colourful hilltribe villages, fantastic shopping and exotic hideaways - and we experience it all on this trip. Witness traditional hilltribe life in a H'mong village, support the rehabilitation of the endangered Asian elephant, step back in time in the ancient kingdom of Sukhothai and try your hand at creating some gastronomic delights. This is your chance to capture the adventure and essence of timeless Thailand.
highlights:
Whip up a culinary storm and taste delicious local dishes in a Thai cooking class in Chiang Mai
Travel like the locals do on an overnight sleeper train, the best way to travel long distances, meet locals and maximise time at destinations
Immerse yourself in the wonders of an ancient tribal culture with a night in the Hmong Lodge, treated to a BBQ dinner and Hmong Cultural show
Make some new pachyderm pals at the unique Friends of the Asia Elephants Hospital and learn about the great work they do to protect these magnificent creatures
Uncover the ancient charms of Sukhothai as you leisurely cycle around the ruin-filled Historical Park, and feel your own cheerfulness increasing in the city named ‘Rising Happiness’
Pay your respect at the memorials by the infamous ‘Bridge over the River Kwai’ – learn about its dark history and the construction of the death railway in Kanchanaburi during the war
source.itineraries:
Day 1 – Bangkok - Arrival
Sa-wat dee! Welcome to Thailand. Thailand's bustling capital, Bangkok is famous for its tuk tuks, khlong boats and street vendors serving up delicious Thai food. Your adventure begins with a welcome meeting at 6pm on Day 1. Please ask the hotel reception where it will take place.
Overnight in Bangkok

Day 2 – Bangkok - Overnight Train To Chiang Mai
Begin the day with a river cruise down the Chao Phraya River to explore the famous ‘khlongs’ (canals) (approximately 1 hour). Life along these canals seems a world away from the chaotic streets of the capital. Pay a visit to the magnificent Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha. The sprawling royal complex houses numerous ornate structures that highlight the grand architectural traditions of Thailand. The rest of the afternoon is free.
Overnight train
Meals: Breakfast

Day 3 – Chiang Mai
The most vibrant city in northern Thailand, Chiang Mai has many famous temples and an interesting old city area. Renowned for dazzling beauty and extremely welcoming locals, the ‘Rose of the North’ will leave you spellbound. Chances are, you won’t want to leave. Embark on a scenic, winding drive up a mountain (approximately 45 minutes) to one of the country's most stunning temple complexes, Doi Suthep. A 300-step naga-guarded stairway leads you to the temples, and the climb is well worth the effort. The hypnotic atmosphere of chanting Buddhist monks and sweeping views of the city make this a most memorable experience. Your leader can help you to arrange optional activities for your free time today and tomorrow – you can get active with a bicycle tour to discover the city and surrounding countryside from a different perspective, indulge in a Thai massage or a spa treatment, or just read a book by the pool. This evening you’ll enjoy a traditional khantohk dinner while being entertained by Akha, Yao, Lahu, H'mong, Lisu and Karen tribal dances. The term Khantohk comes from many small dishes (khan) served on a small or low table (tohk) that evolved from communal meals with honoured guests.
Overnight in Chiang Mai
Meals: Breakfast / Dinner

Day 4 – Chiang Mai
Discover some of the secrets of Thai cuisine by joining a cookery course. Learn about the main ingredients of Thai cuisine, how they are used and stored and what alternatives you can substitute if you can't get them at home. Questions are welcome and you are provided with a comprehensive book of recipes and ingredient details. For lunch, sit down and feast on the delicious results of your tuition. The meal is usually rounded off with a tasting of seasonal Thai fruit. 
Overnight in Chiang Mai
Meals: Breakfast / Lunch

Day 5 – Chiang Mai - Hmong Lodge
Board a minivan for the drive north to the Hmong Hilltribe Lodge, set in picturesque hilly countryside (approximately 1.5 hours). Set in a peaceful valley of a scenic mountain range and surrounded by stunning natural landscapes of jungle with misty mountain views, the Hmong lodge offers a unique and tranquil experience. It's a great escape from the hustle and bustle of busy tourist spots. The rooms are simple and rustic, fitting perfectly with the natural environment. Be sure to pack a warm jumper as the weather will be mild and cool weather year-round due to the lofty mountain locale. The Hmong are an ethnic minority in Thailand who originated in the south of China. Today they comprise the second largest hilltribe group in Thailand. After a barbeque dinner in the lodge's open-air dining area, the day concludes with a cultural performance by the Hmong people. You'll gain an insight into the traditional lifestyle of the tribe, with a wedding ceremony enactment, shamanic ritual and makong (cotton ball) throwing.
Overnight in Hmong Lodge
Meals: Breakfast / Dinner

Day 6 – Hmong Lodge - Sukhothai
Depart the hilltribe village this morning and head on to Lampang (approximately 2 hours). Lampang, also known locally as 'mueang rot ma' meaning Horse Carriage City, is considered by some Thais as the last paradise in Thailand. Here you’ll pay a visit to the Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre, the first elephant hospital in the world established to care for sick and abused elephants. They aim to protect and conserve the welfare of elephants both domesticated and wild, and preserve the animals' natural habitat and lifestyle. You’ll learn more about this important initiative and become acquainted with some of its resident patients. After spending time with the elephants, farewell your new pachyderm pals and head to Sukhothai (approximately 3.5 hours) for the night.
Overnight in Sukhothai
Meals: Breakfast

Day 7 – Sukhothai - Kanchanaburi
Located on a fertile plain, Sukhothai was established in the 13th century as one of the first ancient capitals of Siam, and the name means the 'Dawn of Happiness'. It’s now famous for its World Heritage-listed historic park that celebrates the Golden Age of Thai civilisation. Head out to the historical ruins of Old Sukhothai, set amid beautiful lakes and gardens. The religious art and architecture of the Sukhothai era are considered to be the most classic of Thai styles, and the Sukhothai Historical Park contains the remains of 21 historic sites, with awe-inspiring Buddha images and four large ponds often filled with stunning lotus flowers in full bloom. Upon arrival at the park, hire bicycles and enjoy a few leisurely hours feeling the breeze in your hair and learning about the history of this fascinating place. Enjoy a home-cooked picnic lunch somewhere along the way, and if you have enough free time, visit a local ceramics factory. You’ll then hop on a private minibus south to Kanchanaburi (approximately 6 hours). Located where the Khwae Noi and Khwae Yai rivers converge, Kanchanaburi is home to the infamous 'Bridge on the River Kwai'.
Overnight in Kanchanaburi
Meals: Breakfast / Lunch

Day 8 – Kanchanaburi
This morning you’ll get an insight into the darker side of Kanchanaburi’s history with a moving visit to the Hellfire Pass Memorial, built to honour the Allied POWs and Asian conscripts who died while constructing some of the most difficult stretches of the Thai-Burma Death Railway. You can head out to a teak observation deck and look across to Myanmar just 25 miles away. You’ll also see the eponymous pass, cut through rock 18 metres deep, that got its name from the hellish fires used to light the work at night. Boarding at Nam Tok station, the main terminal of the Death Railway, take a ride along the historic tracks along the Kwai Noi River and travel over the original wooden viaduct (the Bridge on the River Kwai) constructed by the allied POWs. Pass through magnificent scenery and spend a moment reflecting on those who were forced to give their lives in the process of bending this environment to man’s will. Tonight you can explore the rows of street vendors in town and grab a drink overlooking the River Kwai.
Overnight in Kanchanaburi
Meals: Breakfast

Day 9 – Kanchanaburi - Bangkok
Return to the bustling capital Bangkok by private minivan today (approximately 3 hours). The rest of the day (until the evening) is free
Overnight in Bangkok
Meals: Breakfast

Day 10 – Bangkok - Departure
There are no activities planned for the final day and you are able to depart the accommodation at any time.
Meals: Breakfast

page.name: Thailand: Bangkok, Chiang Mai & Kanchanaburi — 10 Days
page.subtitle: Northern temples, hilltribe culture, Death Railway history, and a cooking class in Chiang Mai across 10 days by train, minivan, and bicycle.
page.summary: This 10-day route moves through Thailand's three most distinct regions: Bangkok's river life and palace architecture, Chiang Mai's temple complexes and northern hilltribe territories, and Kanchanaburi's war history along the River Kwai. You'll spend nights in a Hmong village lodge in the mountains north of Chiang Mai, cycle through the 13th-century ruins of Sukhothai's historical park, study Thai cooking techniques in a Chiang Mai kitchen, visit an elephant hospital in Lampang, and travel the Death Railway tracks over the Bridge on the River Kwai. An overnight sleeper train connects Bangkok to Chiang Mai, and a private minivan handles the longer southern legs. Guides are local English speakers, and meals—including a khantohk dinner with tribal performances and a home-cooked picnic in Sukhothai's gardens—are built into each day's rhythm.
highlights: Khao Phraya River cruise and Grand Palace complex in Bangkok, including the Temple of the Emerald Buddha
Doi Suthep temple complex: 45-minute mountain drive from Chiang Mai, accessed by 300-step naga-guarded stairway with city views
Thai cooking class in Chiang Mai: learn ingredient preparation, storage, and substitutions; prepare and eat a full lunch
Overnight stay in a Hmong Lodge in the mountains north of Chiang Mai, with traditional barbecue dinner and cultural performance
Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre in Lampang: hands-on time with rescued and rehabilitated elephants
Sukhothai Historical Park: bicycle tour of 21 historic sites, Buddha images, lakes, and lotus ponds from the 13th-century Golden Age
Hellfire Pass Memorial: World War II site honouring Allied POWs and Asian conscripts; observation deck overlooking Myanmar 25 miles away
Death Railway journey: ride original wooden viaduct over the Bridge on the River Kwai between Nam Tok and Kanchanaburi stations
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Bangkok
Welcome to Bangkok. Thailand's capital centres on the Chao Phraya River, where longtail boats navigate the khlongs—canal networks that run parallel to main streets. A welcome meeting is scheduled at your hotel at 6 p.m., where your guide will brief you on the itinerary and logistics for the week ahead.

Day 2 — Chao Phraya River, Grand Palace & Overnight Train to Chiang Mai
Start with a one-hour river cruise down the Chao Phraya, observing the khlongs and waterside life. You will visit the Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha—a royal complex with ornate structures built in Thai architectural traditions. The afternoon is free. In the evening, board the overnight sleeper train north to Chiang Mai. You will arrive in the north the following morning.

Day 3 — Doi Suthep Temple & Tribal Performances in Chiang Mai
Chiang Mai is the regional centre of northern Thailand, known for its temples and historic old city. This morning, a 45-minute drive ascends the mountain to Doi Suthep, a major temple complex. A 300-step stairway with naga (serpent) railings leads to the temple structures, offering views of the city and access to the courtyard where Buddhist monks chant. The afternoon offers flexibility. Your leader can help arrange optional activities: a bicycle tour through the city and countryside, a traditional Thai massage, or rest at the hotel. This evening, a khantohk dinner is served—a traditional meal where multiple small dishes are presented on low tables. Performances by Akha, Yao, Lahu, Hmong, Lisu, and Karen dancers accompany the meal. Overnight in Chiang Mai. Meals: Breakfast / Dinner

Day 4 — Thai Cooking Class in Chiang Mai
Spend the day in a hands-on Thai cooking course. You will learn the main ingredients used in Thai cuisine, their storage, and available substitutions. You will prepare several dishes and eat lunch of your own cooking. A tasting of seasonal Thai fruit is typically included. A comprehensive recipe book and ingredient guide are provided. The rest of the day is free.

Day 5 — Minivan to Hmong Lodge in the Northern Mountains
A 1.5-hour minivan journey carries you north into hilly countryside to the Hmong Hilltribe Lodge, set in a mountain valley surrounded by jungle. The Hmong are an ethnic minority group now the second-largest hilltribe population in Thailand. Lodge rooms are rustic and designed to fit into the local landscape. Cool mountain weather year-round requires a warm layer. After a barbecue dinner in the open-air dining area, the Hmong people offer a cultural performance including a wedding ceremony enactment, a shamanic ritual, and the makong (cotton ball) throwing game. Overnight at Hmong Lodge.

Day 6 — Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre & Journey to Sukhothai
Depart the hilltribe lodge and drive two hours to Lampang, known locally as 'Horse Carriage City.' The Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre, the first hospital dedicated to treating sick and abused elephants, is located here. You will spend time observing elephant residents and learning about rehabilitation work. Continue south to Sukhothai by minivan, approximately 3.5 hours.

Day 7 — Sukhothai Historical Park by Bicycle
Sukhothai was founded in the 13th century as one of Siam's first capitals. The World Heritage-listed historical park contains the remains of 21 historic sites. The park sits on a fertile plain with lakes and gardens. Upon arrival, you will hire bicycles and spend several hours riding through the ruins, observing Buddha images and religious architecture of the Sukhothai era. A home-cooked picnic lunch is arranged along the route. An optional visit to a local ceramics factory can be arranged. Late afternoon, board a private minivan south toward Kanchanaburi, approximately 6 hours. Kanchanaburi sits where the Khwae Noi and Khwae Yai rivers converge.

Day 8 — Death Railway, Hellfire Pass & Bridge on the River Kwai
This morning you visit the Hellfire Pass Memorial, built to honour Allied prisoners of war and Asian conscripts who died constructing the Thai-Burma Death Railway during World War II. The pass is cut 18 metres deep through rock; it earned its name from fires used to light night work shifts. Boarding at Nam Tok station, you will ride historic tracks along the Khwae Noi River and cross the original wooden viaduct known as the Bridge on the River Kwai, constructed by Allied prisoners. The evening is free to visit the town or rest by the river. Meals: Breakfast

Day 9 — Kanchanaburi to Bangkok
A three-hour private minivan journey returns you to Bangkok. The remainder of the day is free. Overnight in Bangkok. Meals: Breakfast

Day 10 — Bangkok Departure
Breakfast is included. You depart at your own pace.

source.name: Tibet Encompassed
source.summary: To make the pilgrimage to and circumambulation of Mount Kailash is one of the most sacred journeys in the world. The trip itself is one of the most fantastic you can make – starting in the heart of China travel to Lhasa; city of colour and life – monasteries, teahouses, markets and people. From the beauty of central Tibet head west across the vastness of the Tibetan Plateau to where Kailash stands alone. Here join the pilgrims on their kora before turning south to Mount Everest (home to a fairly minor deity) and then on to Kathmandu.
source.itineraries:
Day 1 Beijing Arrival & Beijing Duck Dinner
Nihao! Welcome to Beijing, the capital of China. Your tour begins with a welcome meeting at 6 pm in your hotel lobby. Your guide will go over more details about your trip including meeting up with your guides in each city. This evening take an orientation walk around the hotel area followed by a Beijing Duck dinner.

Accommodation:
•Chongwenmen Hotel or similar (2 nights)
Meals Included:
•Beijing Duck dinner
Day 2 Beijing Great Wall of China at Mutianyu
Travel about 2 hours out of Beijing to the Mutianyu Great Wall. This is one of the best-preserved and restored sections so it is easy to climb, but you can still appreciate the difficulty of its construction. A picnic lunch on the Wall is provided.
Return to Beijing in time for a fantastic acrobatic show.

Accommodation:
• Chongwenmen Hotel or similar (2 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 3 Explore Tiananmen Square, the Forbidden City and Hutongs, train to Xi'an
There will be a lot of walking today as well as using the subway to get around some of Beijing’s most famous sights. Tiananmen Square, one of the world's largest public squares, is home to the Monument of the People's Heroes and the Great hall of the People. From here enter the Forbidden City (built 1406-1420), the ceremonial and political center of the Chinese government for more than 500 years. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 1987 and is listed by UNESCO as the most extensive collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world.
After the Forbidden City, stroll through the alleys formed by lines of traditional courtyards known as Hutong and experience the local lifestyle of Old Beijing.
In the evening, head to the train station for overnight train to Xi’an.
Accommodation:
• Overnight on soft sleeper train Beijing-Xi’an (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 4 Xi'an - Terracotta Warriors, Muslim Quarter
Arriving in Xi’an head to the hotel for breakfast. First on our Xi’an itinerary are the Terracotta Warriors. This incredible archaeological find, discovered in 1976, comprises more than 6,000 warriors, chariots and horses - each individually sculpted from clay with different costumes, height and even facial expressions – all in battle formation. 3 main pits displaying over 2,000 of the warriors are open for you to view.
After lunch in a local village visit one of the best-preserved old residences in Xi’an dating back 400 years. The courtyard was home to seven generations of the Gao family – notable officials of the royal court. Get a taste of the traditional local lifestyle through period furniture, pottery, porcelain, and paintings.
Later, in Xi’an city, wander around the Muslim Quarter with its narrow streets lined with small shops, markets and restaurants.

Accommodation:
• Manxin Hotel Bell Tower or similar ( 2 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 5 Train to Lhasa
This morning we will board the train to Lhasa. The Qinghai-Tibet railway (Xining to Lhasa) is one of China’s greatest engineering feats. It is the highest railway in the world, crossing the high altitude Changtang Plateau – the highest pass is 5069m.
From Xi’an the route travels northeast to Xining, then west to Golmud before turning south to Lhasa. The whole trip from Xi’an takes about 31 hours.

Accommodation:
• Overnight on train Xi’an-Lhasa (1 night)
Meals Included:
•Breakfast
Day 6 Across the Tibetan Plateau to Lhasa
Wake to find yourself well inside Tibet as you travel across the Tibetan Plateau. The passes may be covered by snow at any time of year and in summer the lakes are surrounded by vast grasslands.
On arrival at Lhasa station, on the outskirts of the city, you are warmly welcomed with a pure white katak (prayer scarf). There will be time to relax and adjust to the altitude before a late afternoon orientation walk.

Accommodation:
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Meals Included:
• Dinner
Day 7 Jokhang Temple, Sera Monastery
Start the day with a visit to the Jokhang; the spiritual heart and most sacred temple of Tibet which always attracts a steady stream of pilgrims. Spend some time exploring this large World-Heritage listed site and learn of its rich history. According to legend, the temple was built over a lake after many failed attempts to build monasteries in other nearby locations. Feast your eyes on the golden Buddha which stands in the center. After the visit join the pilgrims walking around the Barkhor Street (in a clockwise direction) considered a sacred kora by Tibetans.
Then, in the late afternoon, we will visit the great university monastery of Sera where you will witness lively philosophical debating (except Sundays).

Accommodation:
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 8 Lhasa Potala Palace
One of the most iconic structures ever built; the Potala Palace was the seat of government and winter residence of the successive Dalai Lamas. A visit is an awe-inspiring experience. Perched 130meters above the city, it is divided into two parts, the White Palace (secular) and the Red Palace (religious - home to chapels, shrines, and tombs of Dalai Lamas). Although you must stick with your guide whilst exploring, this in no way lessens the impact of seeing what is a true architectural wonder.
Free afternoon to explore the city.

Accommodation:
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 9 Lhasa/Gyantse -- Khambala Pass, Yamdrok Lake, Karola Pass, Gyantse Dzong
Today we will drive to Gyantse and there will be many photo stops as this is a spectacular route. From the top of the Khamba-la (4750m) the views of the beautiful turquoise lake, Yamdrok Tso, are superb. Descent to skirt the lake before climbing again to the Karo-la (5045m) for a close-up view of NojinGangzang glacier.
Arriving in Gyantse take a walk around to explore the town and hike up to the Dzong (fort) from where you will have fantastic views of the town and surrounding countryside.

Accommodation:
• Gyantse Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 10 Pelkor Choede Monastery, to Shigatse, Tashilumpo
Pelkhor Choede Monastery was founded by the King of Gyantse in the C15th. It does not belong to a specific tradition of Tibetan Buddhism and whilst much reduced from its original size it remains a very active center. Within the complex stands Gyantse Kumbum (meaning 100,000 images), it is an eight-story structure containing a seemingly endless series of tiny chapels full of Buddhist images – Buddhas, demons, protectors, and saints.
A short drive through small villages to Shigatse, Tibet's second-largest city. Upon arrival, we will first visit the Tashilumpo Monastery, home to the Panchen Lamas. Tour the buildings, each with their own intricate decorations, legends and religious imagery. After that, you can opt to do a “kora” around the monastery or visit the local market.
Accommodation:

Accommodation:
• Tangka Hotel Shigatse or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 11 Shigatse/Sakya/Lhatse – drive Shigatse to Lhatse via Sakya Gompa
It is about 3 hours to the Tibetan town of Sakya; site of Sakya Gompa and birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect of Tibetan Buddhism and very distinctive in its colouring. It is also known as the “second Dunhuang,” for its huge collection of over 40,000 volumes of sacred Buddhist scripts, and just one single, long bookshelf holds around 10,000 ancient scriptures.
After the guided monastery tour take an optional hike up the hillside to visit a small nunnery.
Then we will continue on to Lhatse and overnight in this small town.

Accommodation:
• Vienna Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 12 Lhatse to Saga
It is about 4.5 hours drive to Saga. The surrounding grasslands support a wealth of bird life as well as rarer Tibetan antelope, wild Yak … Roads in Tibet are under continual development and are quite different from what you might expect. Virtually all roads you will travel are paved, but there can be delays due to road works (the climactic extremes make maintenance ongoing).
Arrive early in the afternoon to the typical Chinese and Tibetan town of Saga (4640m). Saga is an important stop-off point on the way to Mount Kailash and is always busy with pilgrims and tourists.

Accommodation:
• Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 13 Saga/Darchen-driving west, first views of Mt Kailash & Lake Manasarovar
Another travel day across the vast highland plain toward Darchen, our base for the kora trek. All day the views are of the great Himalayan range to the south and, to the north, the vast dry Changtang Plateau (which turns briefly and stunningly green with the summer monsoon) and which is home to nomads whose lifestyle remains almost unchanged by the centuries. In the afternoon you will be rewarded with the first spectacular views of Mt Kailash and Lake Manasarovar.
Arrive at Manasarovar Lake, one of the holiest lakes in the world, in the late afternoon. Sacred to Buddhist, Bonpo, Hindu and Jain; every year it receives thousands of pilgrims from all corners of Tibet and India. From the lake several prominent peaks are visible, including Gurla Mandata (7694m). We will continue to drive to Darchen (4675m), a small town and the starting point of the Mt Kailash kora.

Accommodation:
• Chengbao Hotel Darchen or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 14 Kailash Kora - Trek to Dirapuk Monastery
In the morning, take the shuttle bus from Darchen to Sarshung Valley where we will we start our trek. Walk the path with pilgrims who have saved money their whole lives for this moment. After 4 hours we reach Tamdin (4780m) where nomad tents serve a simple lunch and boiled water. From here it is only 4km to Dirakpuk monastery, but this stretch has the some of the best scenery of the entire kora. Dirakpuk (5210m), located on the north side of the Lha-chu River facing the north face of Mt. Kailash was rebuilt in 1985. The name of Dirakpuk originates from the word Dira which means female yak horn and Puk a cave. Legend says a female yak opened the cave. We will visit Drirapuk and stay overnight in a basic local guesthouse.

Accommodation:
• Dirapuk Guesthouse (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 15 Kailash Kora - Trek from Dira Phuk to Zutrul Puk Monastery
Today is the most challenging part of the kora as we cross the Drolma-la (5630m). Although not too long or steep an ascent, it feels very tough due to the altitude. Climbing to the Drolma-la the many pilgrims on the kora will undergo a symbolic death until they reach the pass and are symbolically reborn. One of the most difficult sections of the Drolma-la is the very steep descent once you have crossed the pass – take care! Finally reaching the valley floor we rest and have lunch at Shabjay Dakpo nomad tent. It is then a long, but flat, hike down the valley to Zutrul Phuk monastery where we overnight in the local guest house.

Accommodation:
• Zutrul Puk Guesthouse (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 16 Kailish Kora - Trek from Zutrul Phuk to Darchen, Drive to Lake Manasarovar
Today is an easy walk back to Darchen to complete the Kailash kora. From Zutrul Puk follow the ever- widening valley alongside lines of mani walls and prayer flags. After reaching Darchen make the short drive back to Lake Manasarovar where you will overnight at a guest house near the lake.

Accommodation:
• Guesthouse Manasarovar ( 1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 17 Lake Manasarovar/Saga - return journey across the Tibetan Plateau
Retrace the outward drive back to Saga for the night.

Accommodation:
• Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 18 south across the grasslands towards the Himalaya, Rombuk & Everest Views
From Saga turn south across the grasslands surrounding lake Paiku-tso. Crossing the Friendship Highway it is a steep climb to Rombuk; a day of stunning scenery. The world’s highest monastery, at 5000m, was first built in 1902 by a Nyingma Lama and originally housed more than 500 monks. Today, only about 50 monks and nuns remain, sharing a prayer hall, but maintaining separate residences. The nuns here are great fun and will be delighted to have you join their evening prayers. From here the view is directly up the valley to Base Camp and Qomolangma/Mount Everest (8849m).

Accommodation:
• Rombuk guesthouse ( 1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 19 Rombuk/Kyirong - Tasuwa border
Today is another long days’ drive of 350km. It will take 6-7 hours to get to Kyirong where we spend the night before crossing the border to Nepal.

Accommodation:
• Kyirong Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Dinner
Day 20 Kyirong-Rasuwa, to Kathmandu
This morning after breakfast, we will cross the border from China to Nepal. This can be a slow process, especially the Nepal side.
Namaste! Welcome to Nepal. It is a long day’s drive to Kathmandu, much of the road in very bad condition. Explore this alluring city on a walking tour with your local leader. Check out the Newari architecture at Durbar Square, the vast plaza opposite the old Royal Palaces if time permit.

Accommodation:

Meals Included:

There are no activities planned for today and you can depart at any time.

page.name: Tibet: Beijing to Kathmandu — 21 Days
page.subtitle: From the Great Wall and Forbidden City through the Tibetan Plateau to Mount Kailash, Lake Manasarovar, and Mount Everest
page.summary: This journey moves from China's imperial centers across one of the world's highest plateaus to stand at the foot of Mount Kailash — a mountain held sacred by four religions — and walk the ancient pilgrimage circuit known as the kora alongside devotees who have saved for years to make this crossing. The route begins in Beijing with the Great Wall and Forbidden City, continues by rail to Xi'an and its terracotta warriors, then ascends via the Qinghai-Tibet Railway — the world's highest standard-gauge line — to Lhasa. From there, the itinerary moves west across grassland and high pass to Darchen, the staging point for the kora trek around Mount Kailash. After the kora, the path turns south to Rombuk monastery, the world's highest at 5,000 meters, which sits directly across a valley from Mount Everest's north face. The final descent crosses into Nepal and ends in Kathmandu.
highlights: Walk the Mutianyu section of the Great Wall, one of the best-preserved restored segments near Beijing
Tour the Forbidden City, built 1406–1420 as the political and ceremonial center of imperial China, designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
View the Terracotta Warriors in Xi'an — over 6,000 individually sculpted clay figures discovered in 1976, displayed across three excavated pits
Ride the Qinghai-Tibet Railway at altitudes up to 5,069 meters, the world's highest standard-gauge railway crossing the Changtang Plateau
Visit Jokhang Temple in Lhasa, Tibet's most sacred shrine, and walk the Barkhor Street kora with pilgrims
Visit the Potala Palace in Lhasa, seat of the Dalai Lamas, perched 130 meters above the city with its White Palace and Red Palace
Cross Khambala Pass (4,750 m) for views of turquoise Yamdrok Tso lake and approach Karola Pass (5,045 m) for views of Nojin Gangzang glacier
Visit Tashilumpo Monastery in Shigatse, home to successive Panchen Lamas, with intricate decorations and religious imagery
Tour Sakya Gompa, birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect, known as the 'second Dunhuang' for its collection of over 40,000 volumes of Buddhist scriptures
Complete the three-day kora (circumambulation) of Mount Kailash, trekking from Darchen through Dirapuk and Zutrul Puk monasteries, crossing Drolma-la pass at 5,630 meters
Stay overnight at Rombuk monastery (5,000 m), the world's highest, with direct views up the valley to Mount Everest's north face
Cross the Sino-Nepal border at Kyirong and descend to Kathmandu
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Beijing Arrival and Welcome Dinner
Arrive in Beijing and check into your hotel. At 6 pm, meet your guide in the lobby for a briefing on the 21-day itinerary ahead and logistics for guides and accommodations in each city. Walk the immediate hotel area to orient yourself, then dine on Beijing duck this evening.

Day 2 — Mutianyu Section of the Great Wall
Travel two hours north of Beijing to Mutianyu, one of the best-preserved and restored sections of the Great Wall. The restored stonework makes climbing manageable while the construction's difficulty remains evident. Picnic lunch is served on the wall itself. Return to the city in time for an acrobatic performance.

Day 3 — Tiananmen Square, Forbidden City, and Hutongs — Night Train to Xi'an
A walking-intensive day through central Beijing. Begin at Tiananmen Square, one of the world's largest public plazas, anchored by the Monument of the People's Heroes and the Great Hall of the People. Enter the Forbidden City, built between 1406 and 1420 as the ceremonial and political seat of Chinese government for over 500 years. UNESCO recognizes it as the most extensive collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world and designated it a World Heritage Site in 1987. After touring the palace complex, visit the nearby Hutongs — narrow lanes lined with traditional courtyard residences — to experience the domestic life of historic Beijing. In the evening, transfer to the train station for an overnight soft-sleeper train to Xi'an.

Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Warriors and Muslim Quarter
Arrive in Xi'an and breakfast at the hotel. The morning focuses on the Terracotta Warriors, an archaeological discovery from 1976 comprising over 6,000 life-size clay figures — warriors, chariots, and horses — each individually sculpted with distinct costumes, heights, and facial expressions and arranged in battle formation. Three main excavation pits display more than 2,000 of these figures. After lunch in a local village, visit a 400-year-old residence that housed seven generations of the Gao family, prominent royal court officials. The preserved courtyard displays period furniture, pottery, porcelain, and paintings that convey traditional domestic life. In the city, walk the Muslim Quarter, characterized by narrow streets, small shops, markets, and restaurants.

Day 5 — Qinghai-Tibet Railway: Xi'an to Lhasa
Board the train to Lhasa. The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is one of China's major engineering achievements and the world's highest standard-gauge line. The route from Xi'an travels northeast to Xining, then west to Golmud before turning south toward Lhasa, crossing the high-altitude Changtang Plateau with a highest pass at 5,069 meters. The entire journey takes approximately 31 hours.

Day 6 — Across the Tibetan Plateau to Lhasa
Wake to find yourself well inside Tibet as the train crosses the high Tibetan Plateau. The passes may be covered by snow at any time of year; in summer, the lakes are surrounded by vast grasslands. On arrival at Lhasa station, on the outskirts of the city, you receive a pure white katak (prayer scarf). There will be time to rest and adjust to the altitude before a late afternoon orientation walk, allowing you to begin acclimatizing to Lhasa's elevation while exploring the immediate surroundings.

Day 7 — Jokhang Temple and Sera Monastery
Begin the day at Jokhang, the spiritual heart of Tibetan Buddhism and its most sacred temple. A steady stream of pilgrims moves through this large World Heritage site. The temple's history includes a legend of its construction over a lake after multiple failed attempts to build monasteries at other nearby locations. A golden Buddha stands at the center. After exploring the temple interior, join pilgrims walking clockwise around Barkhor Street, a ritual circuit considered sacred in Tibetan practice. In the late afternoon, visit Sera, a major monastic university, to witness philosophical debates among monks (except on Sundays).

Day 8 — Potala Palace and Lhasa
The Potala Palace commands the Lhasa skyline from 130 meters above the city — a major architectural achievement. This former seat of government and winter residence of successive Dalai Lamas divides into two distinct sections: the White Palace, devoted to secular administration, and the Red Palace, housing religious spaces, chapels, shrines, and the tombs of the Dalai Lamas. A guide accompanies you through the palace's ornate interior. The afternoon opens for independent exploration of Lhasa's streets and neighborhoods.

Day 9 — Lhasa to Gyantse: High Passes and Yamdrok Lake
Drive to Gyantse with planned photo stops along the route. From Khambala Pass (4,750 m), views extend across the turquoise waters of Yamdrok Tso lake. Descend to skirt the lake's edge, then climb again to Karola Pass (5,045 m) for views of Nojin Gangzang glacier. Upon arrival in Gyantse, walk the town, then hike up to the Dzong (fort) for views across town and surrounding countryside.

Day 10 — Gyantse to Shigatse: Pelkor Choede and Tashilumpo Monastery
Visit Pelkhor Choede Monastery, founded by the King of Gyantse in the 15th century. Unlike other Tibetan monasteries, it does not align with a single Buddhist tradition and is now much reduced from its original size but remains an active center. Within the complex stands Gyantse Kumbum, an eight-story structure containing numerous small chapels filled with Buddhist images — Buddhas, protective deities, and saints. Drive through small villages to Shigatse, Tibet's second-largest city. Upon arrival, tour Tashilumpo Monastery, home to successive Panchen Lamas, with buildings featuring intricate decorations, religious legends, and imagery. You may choose to walk the kora circuit around the monastery or visit the local market.

Day 11 — Shigatse to Lhatse via Sakya Gompa
Drive three hours to Sakya, site of Sakya Gompa and birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect of Tibetan Buddhism. The gompa's distinctive architecture sets it visually apart. It holds a significant collection of Buddhist sacred texts housed in the monastery library. After a guided monastery tour, there is an optional hike uphill to visit a small nunnery. Continue onward to Lhatse, a small town where you overnight.

Day 12 — Lhatse to Saga across High Grassland
A 4.5-hour drive carries you across the Tibetan plateau to Saga (4,640 m), an important waypoint for pilgrims heading toward Mount Kailash. The surrounding grasslands support varied birdlife and rare sightings of Tibetan antelope and wild yak. Most roads across Tibet are paved, though ongoing development and harsh climatic extremes mean maintenance work can cause delays — a reminder that infrastructure here is constantly evolving. You arrive early afternoon in this typical Chinese and Tibetan town. The altitude here is significant; take time to acclimatize. You stay at Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar. Breakfast and lunch are included.

Day 13 — Saga to Darchen: First Views of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar
Continue west across the vast highland plain toward Darchen, the base for the Kailash kora trek. The landscape frames views of the Himalayan range to the south and the dry Changtang Plateau to the north, which briefly turns green during the summer monsoon. The plateau is home to nomadic communities whose lifestyle has remained largely unchanged for centuries. In the afternoon, you reach views of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar. One of the holiest lakes in the world, Manasarovar is sacred to Buddhist, Bonpo, Hindu, and Jain traditions and receives thousands of pilgrims annually from across Tibet and India. Several prominent peaks are visible from the lake, including Gurla Mandata (7,694 m). Continue to Darchen (4,675 m), the small town serving as the starting point for the Kailash kora.

Day 14 — Kailash Kora: Darchen to Dirapuk Monastery
Take a shuttle bus from Darchen to Sarshung Valley to begin the kora trek. Walk alongside pilgrims on this sacred circuit. After four hours, reach Tamdin (4,780 m), where nomad tents serve simple lunch and boiled water. From here, walk 4 kilometers to Dirapuk monastery. Dirapuk (5,210 m) sits on the north side of the Lha-chu River facing Mount Kailash's north face. Rebuilt in 1985, the monastery's name derives from 'Dira' (female yak horn) and 'Puk' (cave). Overnight in a basic local guesthouse.

Day 15 — Kailash Kora: Crossing Drolma-la Pass to Zutrul Puk
Today presents the kora's most challenging section. Cross Drolma-la pass (5,630 m), not exceptionally steep or long but demanding due to altitude. The descent after the pass is notably steep; care is needed. Once in the valley floor, rest and have lunch at a Shabjay Dakpo nomad tent. A long, flat hike down the valley leads to Zutrul Phuk monastery, where you overnight in a local guesthouse.

Day 16 — Kailash Kora: Return to Darchen and Lake Manasarovar
Walk the final section of the kora back to Darchen. From Zutrul Puk, follow the widening valley past lines of mani walls and prayer flags. Upon reaching Darchen, complete the three-day circuit. Drive the short distance to Lake Manasarovar, staying overnight at a guesthouse near the shore.

Day 17 — Manasarovar to Saga: Return Across the Tibetan Plateau
Retrace the outward drive back across the Tibetan Plateau to Saga for the night. Accommodation at Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar. Breakfast and lunch included.

Day 18 — Saga to Rombuk: Mount Everest and High-Altitude Monastery
Turn south from Saga across grasslands surrounding Lake Paiku-tso. Cross the Friendship Highway and climb steeply toward Rombuk in a day of varied scenery. Rombuk sits at 5,000 meters as one of the world's highest monasteries, first built in 1902 by a Nyingma Lama and originally housing over 500 monks. Today, approximately 50 monks and nuns remain, sharing a prayer hall but maintaining separate residences. The nuns are welcoming and may invite you to join evening prayers. From the monastery, views extend directly up the valley toward Everest Base Camp and Qomolangma/Mount Everest (8,849 m).

Day 19 — Rombuk to Kyirong: Border Approach
A long 350-kilometer drive stretches across six to seven hours, carrying you toward Kyirong. You'll overnight here at Kyirong Hotel or similar, resting before tomorrow's border crossing into Nepal. Breakfast and dinner are included.

Day 20 — Border Crossing and Descent to Kathmandu
After breakfast, cross from China into Nepal. Border procedures can be slow, particularly on the Nepal side. Welcome to Nepal. The descent to Kathmandu is a long drive on roads in variable condition. Upon arrival, take a walking tour to see Durbar Square, a vast plaza opposite the old Royal Palaces, and observe Newari architecture if time allows.

Day 21 — Depart Kathmandu
No activities are scheduled for today. You are free to depart Kathmandu at any time that suits your travel plans. Breakfast is included.
